hazards.name: A Falling Star's Memories
hazards.notes: The shaft walls vanish and are replaced by an endless field of stars in all direction, as if the viewer were suddenly lost in outer space.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star
hazards.disable: DC 40 Arcana (master) to unweave the magic left in the wake of the Trinity Star’s passage, DC 43 Thievery (expert) to etch temporary runes to siphon away the magic, or dispel magic (8th rank; counteract DC 33) to counteract the magic; three successes are required to disable the trap. Once the PCs are within the trap’s overwhelming illusion, they can still attempt these checks to disable it, but the check DCs increase by 2.
hazards.reset: The trap resets automatically

hazards.name: Abyss-Warped Trees
hazards.notes: A forest of fiendish trees swing their branches and shift their roots to bludgeon and trip creatures in the tainted grove (area A21).
hazards.stealth: DC 12 (Trained) to determine the trees can move
hazards.disable: DC 22 Survival (trained) to find a location the trees can't reach or DC 24 Religion to recite a prayer that temporarily casts out the fiendish energy inside a single tree in the grove, disabling it for 1 minute. A disabled or destroyed tree creates a 5-foot-square area in the grove that's safe from this hazard.
hazards.reset: The Abyss-warped trees cease moving 1 minute after no living creatures are in the tainted grove. They reset immediately. A disabled tree reanimates after 1 minute. A destroyed tree regrows after 1 month.

hazards.name: Acid Mist
hazards.notes: A golden guardrail sprays magical, flesh-eating acid throughout the stairwell.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 26 (expert) to deactivate the trap’s sensors, or Arcana DC 24 (expert) to disrupt the guardrail’s magic, or dispel magic (3rd rank; counteract DC 24) to counteract the guardrail
hazards.reset: The trap automatically deactivates after 1 minute. It resets in 1 hour.

hazards.name: Acid Strongbox Trap
hazards.notes: An invisible magic field around the strongbox releases a spray of acid when disturbed.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Thievery (expert) to harmlessly bleed away the magical field or dispel magic (2nd level; counteract DC 20) to dispel it.

hazards.name: Acidic Needle Launcher
hazards.notes: A ceiling-mounted launcher rains resinous needles onto intruders, after which the needles melt into acid.
hazards.disable: Thievery (DC 36) to disable some firing mechanisms, making three adjacent squares in the trapped area safe to enter.

hazards.name: Aethusa's Prison
hazards.notes: A roiling sphere of chromatic energy floats above a pedestal marked with arcane symbols.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Nature (legendary) or DC 45 Crafting (master) to remove an immunity the prison currently has to one of the following damage types: acid, cold, electricity, or fire (this effect lasts until the prison uses its Energy Immunity reaction to regain that immunity); DC 42 Arcana (master) to fortify the pedestal’s containment runes, preventing the prison from using its Chromatic Eruption action for 1 round and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts 20 damage (this damage bypasses the prison’s hardness and immunities); DC 42 Thievery (master) or dispel magic (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to suppress the pedestal’s containment runes for 1 round, preventing the prison from using its Self-Repair action and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts 20 damage (this damage bypasses the prison’s hardness and immunities). Unlike most hazards, Aethusa’s prison can’t be disabled, but it can be destroyed by reducing it to 0 Hit Points.
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and then resets automatically when it repairs to its maximum Hit Points.

hazards.name: Agitated Carnivorous Plants
hazards.notes: Many carnivorous plants that were once kept satiated now hunger for any meat they can get, even lashing out onto the path to get it.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind
hazards.disable: DC 25 Survival (trained) to distract or trick the plants or DC 22 Nature (expert) to calm the plants

hazards.name: Air Rift
hazards.notes: A portal to the Plane of Air rips open onstage, causing roaring winds to tear through the opera house.
hazards.stealth: +22 (master) to notice the sudden breeze in the theater
hazards.disable: DC 38 Arcana (master) to sew the magical threads of the rift shut, DC 40 Nature or Survival (legendary) to open enough windows and doors to reduce its intensity, or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 34) to counteract the air rift

hazards.name: Ancient Apparatus
hazards.notes: A complex device made of multicolored metal that resembles a combination of grinding gears, spider-like legs, and twitching blades, from which emits …
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery to adjust the device's workings so they seize up and no longer function, or DC 21 Religion to focus prayers to a non-evil deity into the device to disrupt its ability to channel ambient faith
hazards.reset: The ancient apparatus reverts to its non-active mode and resets automatically at the end of any round in which there are no obvious targets to attack.

hazards.name: Angry Dead
hazards.notes: The faces of the original dwarven inhabitants of the city appear in the stone and scream in anger.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm
hazards.disable: DC 23 Religion (trained) to ritually pray for the dead or DC 25 Occultism (trained) to exorcise the spirits' anger; a dwarf succeeds at a DC 22 Diplomacy or Intimidation check, asking or ordering the spirits to stand down.
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 round after all living creatures leave the area. After 1 hour, the haunt reactivates. If the haunt is disabled by a <%TRAITS%54%%>dwarf<%END> succeeding at a Diplomacy or Intimidate check, the haunt is destroyed.

hazards.name: Angry Vegetation
hazards.notes: Five large flowers in the weed-choked field unfurl, each dusting pollen onto vines that animate into wemmuths.
hazards.stealth: DC 42 (master) to notice massive buds beneath the other foliage before they open
hazards.disable: DC 48 Nature (master) or DC 48 Performance (legendary) to calm a flower, closing it
hazards.reset: Wemmuths collapse into ordinary vines and the trap resets if the area is left alone for 1 minute.

hazards.name: Anguished Sarenite
hazards.notes: The gold religious symbol of a former priest of Sarenrae is haunted by the priest's tormented soul.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Diplomacy to bring the spirit to its senses, or DC 24 Religion (expert) to banish it
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Animal Pit
hazards.notes: A weight-activated trap door covers a pit that’s 10 feet square and 20 feet deep.
hazards.stealth: DC 18 (DC 14 if the trap has been activated within the last day, or 0 if the trap door is disabled or broken )
hazards.disable: DC 12 Thievery to remove the trap door
hazards.reset: The trapdoors automatically reset to their closed position once a creature falls in, allowing for more creatures to fall in, though any camouflage on the trap door falls in as well, making it easier for creatures to notice the trap door.

hazards.name: Apocalypse Stormfront
hazards.notes: An endless void stretches in all directions. Visions of Golarion’s destruction roll like storm clouds across the space.
hazards.disable: DC 47 Acrobatics to Fly through the space without becoming stuck in the webs, DC 50 Athletics to Climb the webs and make progress forward through the infinite, DC 47 Nature or Occultism or DC 50 Arcana or Religion (legendary) to collapse the extradimensional space, or DC 52 Perception to peer through the visions of Golarion to notice discrepancies that help keep the overwhelming despair from setting in; six successes disables the hazard, causing it to vanish forever and shunting all creatures to Liralarue’s Prison.
hazards.reset: The hazard resets automatically once no creatures are in the area.

hazards.name: Armageddon Orb
hazards.notes: A roiling red orb, forged from a drop of the god Rovagug ’s blood, rains fire from the sky when a specified condition is met.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to imbue a thieves’ toolkit with aspects representing Asmodeus and Sarenrae and use them to drain away the orb’s power over 10 minutes; the character attempting this check takes 5 fire damage each round until the orb is depleted

hazards.name: Arms of the Drowned
hazards.notes: Ghostly arms rise up from the water to clutch and grab, while a geyser of leech-infested water sprays up into the central shrine.
hazards.stealth: +20 (expert) to catch glimpses of ghostly figures drowning in the water below
hazards.disable: DC 20 Religion to offer prayers to calm the haunt, or DC 23 Intimidation to threaten the unquiet spirits away
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates and resets at the start of any round in which the PCs aren’t in the river, on the bridges, or in the shrines, but the leech swarms remain in the shrine for 10 minutes before retreating back into the water below.

hazards.name: Ash Web
hazards.notes: This dangerous sooty black mold readily releases its toxic spores when disturbed. The entire swath of fungus in area B2 is a single organism. There …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City
hazards.disable: Survival DC 27 (expert) to remove a 10-foot-square patch of ash web without triggering the spores
hazards.reset: This large patch of ash web resets automatically at the start of the round.

hazards.name: Auto-Turret
hazards.notes: A mounted gun equipped with a magical targeting system and integrated ammo supply.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #173: Doorway to the Red Star
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 35 (master) to disconnect the turret from its ammo supply system, or Arcana DC 35 (master) to neutralize the magical targeting system. Tan-Takneh can also deactivate one or both auto-turrets remotely with a special command word.

hazards.name: Avalanche Doors
hazards.notes: The double door is a false door; when triggered, the door slams downward like a drawbridge to crush anyone standing before it.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Thievery (trained) to detach the trigger from the doors and lock them in place

hazards.name: Avernal Flashback
hazards.notes: A phantasmal crimson worm appears to rampage outside the workshop, afflicting the area with phantom tremors, blistering heat, and cave-ins.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Athletics , Occultism , or Religion ; it takes three successful checks to weaken the haunt or erect supports that brace the ceiling. A PC who speaks Dwarven can attempt DC 22 Diplomacy (trained) checks to calm the phantasmal cave worm.

hazards.name: Avian Rage
hazards.notes: Hundreds of panicked whippoorwills swarm through the area.
hazards.disable: DC 43 Nature (master) to calm the birds, DC 45 Occultism (master) to alter your aura, or DC 45 Performance (master) to imitate the living
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any undead or creatures with negative healing in the garden.

hazards.name: Axiomatic Polymorph Trap
hazards.notes: A Utopian glyph transforms trespassers into aeons.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (master) to drain the glyph's power harmlessly, or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 42) to counteract the glyph
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Azure Lilies
hazards.notes: The azure lilies expel a burst of toxic pollen.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Nature or Survival (expert) to harvest the plant's pollen without disturbing the blossoms.
hazards.reset: 1 month.

hazards.name: Ballista Defense
hazards.notes: A ballista armed with a massive bolt fires on a creature approaching the Palace.
hazards.disable: DC 36 Thievery (master) to sabotage the ballista by reaching through the firing slit from outside (this DC is reduced by 10 if the PCs are in the room with the ballista), or DC 33 Intimidation to frighten off the Pitax Warden operating the ballista.
hazards.reset: (1 day) If the PCs haven't reached 30 Liberation Points, additional ammunition for a ballista can be secured in a day, but if the PCs have reached 30 Liberation Points, a ballista that runs out of ammo cannot be reset.

hazards.name: Banshee's Symphony
hazards.notes: A magically contagious wail of the banshee spell is trapped in the larynx of an invisible, mummified elf.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 42 (master) to pierce the invisible larynx so precisely that the magic releases in a trickle before the trap activates, Thievery DC 44 (legendary) three times to deconstruct the larynx while the trap is active in such a way that it tears the spell apart, or spell DC 38 (9th level) to counteract the wail of the banshee before the trap activates
hazards.reset: The trap ends when the trap is unable to make a creature scream (usually because no creature failed its save on the previous turn or because all creatures have critically succeeded in the past). It then resets over 24 hours, as a new scream builds up in the mummified larynx.

hazards.name: Barzillai's Hounds
hazards.notes: Hell hounds invisible to all but their lone target burn their chosen victim.
hazards.disable: Religion DC 24 (expert) to perform an exorcism (with 2 actions)
hazards.reset: If their designated target dies or the hounds can't reach it in a turn, the hounds vanish into noxious smoke, but they manifest again elsewhere in the city after the next sunset.

hazards.name: Battering Door
hazards.notes: Animated door slams into trespassers.
hazards.disable: DC 30 Diplomacy or Occultism (master) to soothe the psychic impressions or DC 28 Thievery (expert) to jam the door open
hazards.reset: The trap resets automatically.

hazards.name: Bee-Induced Panic
hazards.notes: Enraged bees spread panic, causing the crowd to trample each other in a desperate attempt to escape.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Diplomacy (expert) to calm the panicked crowd and guide them to safety, DC 20 Medicine (trained) to attend to victims' injuries, or DC 21 Nature (expert) to instruct the crowd on how best to protect themselves from bees. Alternatively, a PC able to communicate with insects can instead attempt a DC 18 Diplomacy (trained) check to calm and redirect the bees. Three successful checks are required to completely disable the hazard. The hazard is automatically disabled after 5 rounds or once both swarms are defeated.

hazards.name: Befuddling Gas Trap
hazards.notes: Seven nozzles hidden within holes in the 15‑foot-high ceiling release a poison gas.
hazards.stealth: +21 (expert) or DC 31 (expert) to notice the hidden override mechanism on the north wall.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Thievery (master) to disable the hidden mechanism on the north wall, immediately sucking the gas from the room, or DC 29 Thievery (expert) to adequately plug one of the seven nozzles. When all seven nozzles are plugged or destroyed, the trap is deactivated.
hazards.reset: After an hour, the trap deactivates; the gas disperses slowly, and the doors can be opened again. After 24 hours, the gas builds up and the trap can be triggered again.

hazards.name: Benefactor's End
hazards.notes: A spectral assailant drives a stake into a dying vampire's heart; the vampire collapses and releases a surge of negative energy.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Religion (expert) to drain away the haunt's negative energy
hazards.reset: Unless disabled, the haunt materializes again on the next moonrise.

hazards.name: Bestial Transformation
hazards.notes: Enchanted carvings of animals transform any creatures who damage the door into the animal they harmed.
hazards.disable: DC 26 Nature (expert) to handle the animal carvings or DC 33 Thievery (master) to scratch out the animal carvings or dispel magic (5th level; counteract DC 28) to counteract the spell
hazards.reset: automatic

hazards.name: Bittersweet Mask
hazards.notes: The many iron bars of this iron mask fits tightly around Javownir’s head and snout, looking almost as if it was built in place to conform …
immunity: precision damage; Special whenever the mask takes damage
Javownir takes the same damage (DC 44 basic Reflex save)
hazards.disable: DC 45 Thievery (expert) twice to find the hidden latches, DC 48 Athletics (master) to wrench the mask open quickly enough to prevent it from triggering before it’s destroyed, dispel magic (9th-rank; counteract DC 35), or automatic with Spleen’s key
hazards.reset: The mask resets automatically at the start of the round after it is triggered.

hazards.name: Black Powder Bomb
hazards.notes: Three bulky kegs of black powder placed at key locations in the temple are triggered to explode in unison, causing the entire structure to collapse …
hazards.stealth: DC 15 (The three powder kegs aren't particularly well hidden, but they are out of sight to casual observation.)
hazards.disable: No special skills are required to disable this manually activated trap. As an Interact action, a PC can sweep aside some black powder to interrupt the fuse line, but this doesn't prevent Gerhard from activating a keg via blunderbuss. A keg that is removed from its position (either by being thrown over the cliff or merely carried away) retains its explosive potential, but as long as one of the three kegs are removed they no longer have the precise placement required to trigger a collapse—an explosion at this point merely inflicts fire damage in the appropriate areas but does not particularly damage the temple structure itself. A keg's contents can be dispersed by scattering the gunpowder to the wind (most efficiently by pouring it over the cliff side) as a 2-action activity, or rendered permanently inert by pouring a gallon of water into the powder, inhibiting its explosive qualities. The kegs themselves can be destroyed with damage (note that the AC listed below for each keg takes into account the fact that Gerhard has wedged the kegs into nooks in the temple's stone flooring and walls), but note that any fire damage (including incidental fire damage from area effects like a fireball or Gerhard's blunderbuss) causes them to explode. At your option, other actions may be similarly effective at disabling this hazard.

hazards.name: Blast Tumbler
hazards.notes: A hard-to-reach rune is placed on the lock’s tumbler. It emits a blast of force when the door is jostled.
hazards.disable: DC 32 Thievery (master) to disarm the rune, or dispel magic (5th level; counteract DC 28) to counteract the rune’s magic.
hazards.reset: The rune resets 1 minute after it triggers.

hazards.name: Blood Drain
hazards.notes: A tiny spark of Nin’s will drains the blood from living intruders.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 26 (expert) to vandalize the space, or Religion DC 24 (expert) to pray to a god for passage, or dispel magic (3rd rank; counteract DC 25) to counteract the magical energy
hazards.reset: The trap automatically deactivates after 1 minute. It resets in 1 hour.

hazards.name: Blood of Belcorra
hazards.notes: A bloody image of Belcorra arises, emits a soul‑draining light, then inhales blood from living creatures in the room.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Thievery (trained) to wipe away enough of the bloodstain to disrupt the haunt’s necromantic energies, or DC 20 Religion (trained) to exorcise the haunt
hazards.reset: If the haunt is disabled or destroyed through damage, the bloody phantom of Belcorra sprays upward in a spiral, dousing the trap door leading to area A25 before draining upward through the keyhole, which reduces the Thievery DC to <%ACTIONS%2412%%>Pick the Lock<%END> to 20. At the next sunrise, the blood drains back down to this room and the haunt resets. The haunt is destroyed permanently once Lasda Venkervale is rescued from area D9.

hazards.name: Blood Tears
hazards.notes: A wailing spirit appears and gouges their own eyes. As they do, blood seeps from the eyes of those who witness the act, obscuring their vision.
hazards.stealth: DC 32 (master) to notice your vision tint red
hazards.disable: DC 30 Diplomacy (master) to talk the spirit out of gouging its eyes or DC 32 Religion (trained) to ease the spirit's sorrows
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Blood-Draining Lock
hazards.notes: A spring-loaded blade hidden in the door’s handle stabs anyone attempting to turn it, dealing unholy wounds that bleed profusely. Disabling or …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 31 (expert) on the spring mechanism

hazards.name: Blood-Soaked Soil
hazards.notes: The blood of those who died in the area bubbles up from the earth, soaking the soil and turning it into a bloody morass.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Diplomacy or Occultism (trained) to settle the spirits or DC 19 Religion (trained) to bless the area
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Bloodletting Snares
hazards.notes: Slender razor wire snags a creature, hauling them up into the air while causing deep, bloody wounds.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Survival (expert) or Thievery (expert) to snip the wire without getting snared

hazards.name: Bloodthirsty Toy
hazards.notes: A scruffy stuffed bear animates, biting whoever disturbs it.
hazards.stealth: DC 17 (trained) to hear a child imitate an animal's roar
hazards.disable: DC 20 Thievery (trained) to handle the toy without disturbing it or DC 21 Occultism (trained) to suppress the memories suffusing the toy
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Bloodthirsty Urge
hazards.notes: An object haunted by the echoes of a vicious mind attempts to kill someone who comes near.
hazards.disable: DC 29 Religion (master) to exorcise the spirit or DC 31 Diplomacy (expert) to talk it down

hazards.name: Blooming Jijioa
hazards.notes: An invisible solar flare causes this patch of unassuming ground cover to suddenly bloom into a radioactive field.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Survival (trained) to remove a 5-foot square of jijioa, or 5 points of fire damage to destroy an affected area
hazards.reset: An hour after blooming, a jijioa patch goes dormant for 1 week.

hazards.name: Boiling Fountains
hazards.notes: Four pressure plates beneath the floorboards activate dragon-headed fountains on either side of the room, which spray boiling water across the area …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace
hazards.stealth: DC 18 (trained) to spot the pressure plates
hazards.disable: DC 21 Thievery (trained) to disable each pressure plate, DC 16 to jam each fountain, or DC 18 to deflect a fountain's spray
hazards.reset: Once a pressure plate has been activated, it must be reset manually

hazards.name: Boneburst
hazards.notes: A low howl rises from the ground, gathering strength as scraps of ancient armor, bone fragments, and clumps of earth rise into the air. Crimson vapor …
hazards.stealth: +38 (master) to notice that clouds of debris are coalescing into swirling, faceless shapes held together by rust-red fog and spectral, dripping clots of gore
hazards.disable: DC 38 Occultism (master) to temporarily negate the psychic resonances around each fragment, causing the agglomeration to fall apart, or DC 33 Religion (expert) to temporarily interrupt Verex-That-Was's unholy power with divine energy from another source. If a boneburst takes 40 points of damage from a single source and it isn't destroyed, it is rendered dormant for 1 round.
hazards.reset: If the boneburst spends 5 consecutive rounds without coalescing around a living creature, it falls dormant, sinking back into the earth. After it falls dormant or is disabled, the boneburst gathers energy over the course of the next hour, after which it can be triggered again.

hazards.name: Bottomless Pit
hazards.notes: An iron trapdoor covers an infinitely deep 10-footsquare pit.
hazards.stealth: DC 30 (or 0 if the trapdoor is disabled or broken) or detect magic
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (trained) to remove the trapdoor
hazards.reset: The trap still causes creatures to fall forever if they fall in, but the trapdoor must be reset manually for the trap to become hidden again.

hazards.name: Boulder Deadfall Trap
hazards.notes: A weight-sensitive plate buried underneath sand pulls a boulder over a cliff ledge, causing it to fall on targets within the entrance.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind
hazards.stealth: DC 25 (trained); DC 0 to spot the balanced boulders
hazards.disable: DC 27 Crafting (expert) or DC 25 Thievery (expert) to find and disconnect the plate from the tipping mechanism
hazards.reset: Resetting the boulders in the trap is a labor-intensive project that takes 2 hours.

hazards.name: Bounding Hounds
hazards.notes: Three phantom hounds chase down intruders, damaging any they pass through.
hazards.disable: DC 36 Nature (expert) to calm each hound, or DC 38 Occultism (master) to banish each hound
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Breakaway Ladder
hazards.notes: The rope ladder rips free from its anchors and drops into the pit.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Thievery (trained) or DC 22 Crafting (trained) to secure the ladder’s anchors so they won’t break

hazards.name: Breath of Blood
hazards.notes: A churning pool of blood bubbles and seethes, periodically venting noxious vapors into the air.
hazards.disable: Three DC 33 Nature or Occult checks to draw from the blood its magical nature, causing it to clot and become inert, a DC 36 Religion check to offer prayers to sever the sacred link to Kabriri, or dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 29) to render the hazard inert for 10 minutes
hazards.reset: The hazard settles back down 1 round after all creatures leave the room and can trigger again at the start of the next round.

hazards.name: Breath of Despair
hazards.notes: The faces carved on the wall appear to inhale, then exhale slithering tendrils of darkness to harm those who would despoil the tomb.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 23 (expert) to disarm the trap's sensors in the chamber floor, or dispel magic (3rd level; counteract DC 23) to counteract the faces. Breaking one of the faces on the walls reduces the trap's save DC, attack rolls, and its total actions by 1 per broken face; if all four faces are destroyed, the trap is disabled.
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Breeg's Traps
hazards.notes: Several dozen spike snares are littered across this hex.
hazards.disable: DC 17 Survival (made as an individual hexploration activity) to locate and disarm all the traps by hand.
hazards.reset: There are enough traps in this hex that this hazard can be triggered up to 5 times before all the traps are used up.

hazards.name: Broken Rebus Attack
hazards.notes: Ghostly attackers knock the tables about, send dishes flying, and pull fleeing creatures into the room.
hazards.disable: DC 34 Religion (expert) to say an Iroran prayer and put the haunt temporarily to rest, DC 38 Occultism (master) to create a ward against future hauntings
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates after 1 minute. It re-forms at the same times every day, 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., which is when the monks had their morning and evening meals. If at least two people cook a meal in the kitchen, share a meal in the refectory, and utter a prayer to Irori before the meal, the haunt becomes permanently disabled and doesn't re-form.

hazards.name: Brooding Fvalthahalia
hazards.notes: Tiny black flames mirror living creatures' movements in the city above as scraps of shadow patrol the streets—flames that notice intruders in their …
hazards.disable: DC 40 Thievery (master) to adjust the model so its attention is focused inward, DC 37 Occultism (expert) to cause the accumulated psychic energy to discharge harmlessly, or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 32). A character who sneaks through the room with a DC 32 Stealth (expert) check avoids triggering the hazard, but this does not disable it.
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Bursting Bone Vault
hazards.notes: This bone-filled vault disgorges its contents the moment the vault door slides open.
hazards.disable: DC 20 Thievery (trained) or Stealth (trained) to carefully open the vault door without disturbing the bones

hazards.name: Button Mash
hazards.notes: The room floods with harmful effects by pressing a magic sigil on a console. Each sigil causes different results. There are six sigils on the console.
hazards.disable: DC 40 Arcana (master) to disenchant each sigil (can be done from either side of the reception desk), DC 43 Thievery (master) twice to disable the console (can only be done while behind the reception desk), or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 40) to counteract each sigil; prevent Noph from pressing the buttons by gaining access to the reception desk or other methods

hazards.name: Buzzing Latch Rune
hazards.notes: An invisible rune on the door begins emitting a very loud buzzing sound, potentially paralyzing an intruder.
hazards.disable: DC 34 Thievery (master) to disrupt the rune without triggering it or dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 31) to magically counteract the rune
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: By the Horns
hazards.notes: The head of the Granite Ox tosses back and forth as the creature charges toward Dhuraxilis.
hazards.disable: DC 27 Athletics (master) to tug one of the ox’s ears, DC 32 Arcana , Nature , Occultism , or Religion (expert) to distract the Ox with a display of magic, or DC 35 Acrobatics (expert) to dangle in front of the Ox’s eyes and obscure its vision; three successes are required to disable the hazard
hazards.reset: The hazard ends automatically after 5 rounds or once all PCs are thrown from the Ox’s back, whichever comes first.

hazards.name: Call of the Void
hazards.notes: A supernatural compulsion to leap into the unknown exerts itself on anyone who approaches the ledge.
hazards.stealth: DC 25 (expert) to notice a slight tugging feeling
hazards.disable: DC 34 Occultism or DC 36 Arcana to expel the magical compulsion from the current island and from any of the red ropes directly attached to it, darkening the rope in color. The Echo also automatically disables the hazard from any island he's standing on, and any of the red ropes directly attached to it, when he Reconstitutes from Thought on that island.
hazards.reset: The call of the void persists as long as the Echo exists, though it doesn't activate until the Echo has rolled initiative. The hazard resets each day.

hazards.name: Camazotz's Swarm
hazards.notes: A massive swarm of bats flies throughout the room, hampering vision, attacking foes, and magically restoring Camazotz’s followers.
hazards.disable: DC 17 Nature (trained) to disperse the swarm or DC 15 Religion (trained) to disrupt Camazotz’s connection, which disperses the swarm
hazards.reset: The swarm disperses and returns to roost throughout the room 1 minute after all enemies leave the room. The swarm recovers 5 Hit Points per day thanks the power of Camazotz.

hazards.name: Camouflaged Spiked Pit
hazards.notes: A 20-foot deep, funnel-shaped pit with dozens of wooden spikes lining its walls.
hazards.disable: Yanking the cloth away is a simple way to expose the danger to allow someone to merely avoid it by walking around its edges, but it cannot be quickly disabled.
hazards.reset: Creatures can still fall into the trap once it has been exposed, but the camouflaged cover must be reset manually for the trap to become hidden again.

hazards.name: Cannibalistic Echoes
hazards.notes: A pack of cannibalistic spirits swarm through the area, devouring living creatures.
hazards.stealth: DC 42 (master) to sense something unusual lurking in the area's echoes
hazards.disable: DC 40 Intimidation (master) to drive the spirits off with a ferocious display or DC 42 Occultism (expert) to exorcise the spirits
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Canopy Drop
hazards.notes: A trapdoor, connected to floor sensors, opens in the section of floor marked on the map, while the surrounding floor suddenly tilts to a 45-degree …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace
hazards.disable: DC 23 Thievery (expert) to jam the mechanisms and keep the trapdoor from opening, or to locate the bypass switch hidden under a stair riser just outside the room

hazards.name: Carnivorous Mold
hazards.notes: Spores explode onto nearby creatures, leaving welts as the mold dissolves exposed flesh.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Religion (legendary) to neutralize the void energy that animates the mold, or DC 36 Survival (master) to remove the mold without triggering the spores

hazards.name: Castigate the Faithless
hazards.notes: Magic forces those who pass by the statue to the ground with sudden force; pressing the bypass button deactivates the trap for 1 minute.
hazards.stealth: DC 47 (master) or DC 50 (legendary) to notice the bypass button hidden in Urgathoa's skeletal feet
hazards.disable: DC 47 Religion (legendary) to deactivate the trap through prayer, dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 47) to counteract the trap, or press the bypass button
hazards.reset: The trap resets automatically if triggered, after 1 minute if the bypass button is pressed, or after 15 minutes if disabled or counteracted.

hazards.name: Catacomb Cave
hazards.notes: The ceiling is unstable, and any Medium or larger creature that approaches within 5 feet of the collapsed tunnel triggers a cave-in.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #151: The Show Must Go On
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 21 (trained) to prop up the ceiling in key locations prior to the cave-in.

hazards.name: Caustic Dart Trap
hazards.notes: Three launching mechanisms built into the mudbrick walls expel darts containing acidic chemicals. All three launching mechanisms must be disabled or …
hazards.stealth: +20 (expert) or DC 30 (expert) to notice the three launching mechanisms built into the wall
hazards.disable: DC 32 Thievery (master) to sufficiently jam the tubes to make the trap unable to attack creatures in a single 5-foot square in the room, or DC 34 Crafting (master) to alter one of the three launching mechanisms
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets 1 minute after no creatures are in area C7.

hazards.name: Caustic Gas Trap
hazards.notes: Pressure plates in the hall trigger the release of caustic gas.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Crafting (master) to neutralize the acid or DC 30 Thievery (master) to disable the pressure plates
hazards.reset: A 10-minute Interact activity and a new supply of caustic gas.

hazards.name: Caustic Vapor
hazards.notes: The door slams shut, and poison gas fills the room.
hazards.disable: Occultism DC 36 (master) or Religion DC 36 (master) to exorcise the spirits
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 day.

hazards.name: Cave-In
hazards.notes: The tunel collapses, filling the passage with stone
hazards.source: Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley, Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown
hazards.disable: DC 25 Survival (trained) to prop up the tunnel ceiling without triggering a collapse

hazards.name: Cave-In
hazards.notes: The rubble shifts and the cavern ceiling collapses.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown, Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley
hazards.disable: DC 28 Crafting (expert) or DC 31 Survival (trained) to prop up the cavern ceiling without triggering a collapse.

hazards.name: Centipede Carcasses Trap
hazards.notes: Three giant centipede carcasses have wire springs that pull out and fling their sharpened legs around the room.
hazards.disable: DC 23 Nature (trained) to bend the centipede carapace so the wire can't pull out any more legs, or DC 21 Thievery (expert) to cut the springy wires. After all three carcasses are disabled (regardless of the check used), the trap is deactivated. The trap automatically deactivates after 10 rounds.

hazards.name: Charge of the Spear Legion
hazards.notes: When triggered, the room lurches suddenly on its side, causing those in the room to slide down toward the double line of spears on the west wall …
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 20 to deactivate the triggering pressure plate near the northern door
hazards.reset: After 1 minute, the chamber rights itself and resets the trap.

hazards.name: Chernasardo Chompers
hazards.notes: These animal snares have been repurposed to discourage unwanted intruders. When a creature steps onto the snare, jaws with sharpened teeth close …
hazards.disable: DC 26 Acrobatics (trained) to step clear the snare before it springs, or DC 22 Thievery (trained) to trigger the trap harmlessly

hazards.name: Choking Tethers
hazards.notes: Three shadow tethers form when a creature reaches the hall's midpoint; each lashes, grabs, and crushes creatures in the hall.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to disable each tether or dispel magic (10th level, counteract DC 48) to counteract each tether

hazards.name: Cleansing Suite
hazards.notes: Deadbolts inside the doors clunk as three glowing runes appear on the ceiling.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Arcana , Nature , Occultism , or Religion to erase the runes, or DC 46 Crafting or Thievery to destroy the runes, or dispel magic (9th rank, counteract DC 41); each rune requires a success to remove (three runes total)
hazards.reset: 1 minute after the hazard activates, the deadbolts unlock and the hazard resets.

hazards.name: Clockwork Dancers
hazards.notes: Several clockwork humanoid figures armed with spinning blades move throughout the area.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 25 (expert) to deactivate the clockworks from the control panel. Two successes are needed to deactivate the trap.
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates after 4 rounds and resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Clone Mirrors
hazards.notes: Two opposing mirrors spawn illusory duplicates of creatures in the hall in an unending tide.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (expert) to reposition each mirror, or dispel magic (3rd level; counteract DC 25) to counteract each mirror
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Cluster Heart
hazards.notes: A wave of magic passes through the area, causing crystal shards to grow and stab intruders.
hazards.stealth: DC 45 (master) to hear or feel the energy coalescing
hazards.disable: DC 45 Nature (master) to chip away at the crystal and disrupt its resonance, or DC 42 Thievery (master) to carefully detach the crystals and then safely smash them
hazards.reset: Once the cluster heart uses its reaction, it automatically resets after 1 minute. As long as the cluster heart has 150 or more Hit Points, it recovers 50 per day.

hazards.name: Cold Spot
hazards.notes: The temperature suddenly drops as spectral forces gather in the area.
hazards.disable: DC 19 Religion (trained) to banish the cold spot with ritual prayers or DC 20 Occultism (trained) to foil the arrival of outside forces
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Collapsing Bridge
hazards.notes: An iron bridge's connectors give way to drop into the lake below.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger, Claws of the Tyrant
hazards.disable: DC 40 Thievery (master) to disable one side of the bridge's quick release mechanisms

hazards.name: Collapsing Bridge
hazards.notes: As a pillar collapses, the bridge itself groans and shakes, then crumbles into the river below.
hazards.source: Kingmaker Companion Guide, Claws of the Tyrant
hazards.stealth: +25 (or 0 if a PC has analyzed the supports and discovered they are on the verge of collapse)
hazards.disable: Several weeks of repair can rebuild the supports and remove the danger; at the GM's discretion, spells like wall of stone or wall of force can be used to augment the supports more quickly, although these spells are likely out of reach of the PCs at this point.

hazards.name: Collapsing Bridge
hazards.notes: Metal supports twist and shear off the bridge, causing stretches of the structure to collapse.
hazards.source: Claws of the Tyrant, Kingmaker Companion Guide, Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger
hazards.disable: DC 40 Engineering Lore to identify and reinforce weak points, DC 43 Crafting (master) to construct secondary supports, or DC 45 Athletics (legendary) to reinforce the bridge with found materials; three successes are required to halt the collapse

hazards.name: Collapsing Cell
hazards.notes: A section of ceiling and iron cell bars collapse inward.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Thievery (trained) or DC 25 Crafting (trained) to use a loose iron bar to shore up the ceiling.

hazards.name: Collapsing Floor
hazards.notes: The westernmost 5 feet of the building gives way, dropping rubble and anyone in the area into the depths of the Lantern Kingdom below.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 51 to quickly jury-rig key supports against weak wall sections to prevent the collapse

hazards.name: Collapsing Structure (Ebeshra)
hazards.notes: Ebeshra brushes against a structure, possibly causing it to collapse.
hazards.stealth: +20 (master) to notice cracks forming in the walls of the structure as Ebeshra approaches
hazards.disable: DC 43 Athletics (master), Crafting (master), or Engineering Lore (master) to brace the structure to reduce the risk of collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
hazards.reset: The building becomes susceptible to Shake Apart again 1d6 rounds after it's stabilized.

hazards.name: Collapsing Structure (Mogaru)
hazards.notes: Mogaru brushes against a structure, severely compromising the building's stability and possibly causing it to collapse.
hazards.stealth: +20 (master) to notice cracks forming in the walls of the structure as Mogaru approaches
hazards.disable: DC 43 Athletics (master), Crafting (master), or Engineering Lore (master) to brace the structure to reduce the risk of collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
hazards.reset: The building becomes susceptible to Shake Apart again 1d6 rounds after it is stabilized.

hazards.name: Color Spray Trap
hazards.notes: A loud pop sounds when this door is opened, followed immediately by a blast of colorful lights that washes over whoever opened the door.
hazards.stealth: DC 22 (trained) to notice the glyph on the doorjamb
hazards.disable: DC 25 Thievery (trained) to disable the glyph, or dispel magic (1st level; counteract DC 22) to counteract the glyph

hazards.name: Compression Tunnel
hazards.notes: This shadow tunnel compresses when creatures pass through.
hazards.disable: DC 46 Athletics (legendary) twice to push back the shadows or DC 48 Thievery (legendary) three times to pierce through the shadows

hazards.name: Confounding Betrayal
hazards.notes: Allies appear to shed their disguises and reveal themselves to be malevolent monsters.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Deception (expert) twice to confound the haunt with your own deceptions, or DC 28 Occultism (trained) twice to create a ward against the haunt’s mental influence
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minute after all creatures leave the area but resets immediately thereafter

hazards.name: Confounding Portal
hazards.notes: Tiny runes carved around a doorframe or on a hall's walls surreptitiously confound creatures into circling the room or hallway they attempted to exit …
hazards.disable: DC 17 Thievery to scratch out the runes, or DC 16 Arcana to destroy the runes
hazards.reset: automatic

hazards.name: Constricting Hall
hazards.notes: A hall's four walls become fluid and elastic when a creature reaches the hall's midpoint.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (trained) to stabilize each wall, or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 26) to counteract each wall
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Consuming Cabinet
hazards.notes: Animated cabinet imprisons intruders. The cabinet has two compartments; each can hold a single Medium creature or two Small-sized creatures or …
hazards.disable: DC 30 Thievery (expert) twice on cabinet; DC 28 Crafting or Thievery (expert) to remove each or two doors
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Conundrum Ward
hazards.notes: A complex geometrical ward with mathematical equations woven into its lines magically seals the door, harming anyone who touches it.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 30 (master) to sabotage the ward, Geometry or Mathematics Lore DC 25 (trained) to calculate the solution to the complex equations, Crafting DC 28 (expert) to manipulate the ward’s precise underlying schematics, or dispel magic (4th rank; counteract DC 26) to counteract the magical ward
hazards.reset: The trap automatically resets after being triggered. If disabled, the ward does not reset.

hazards.name: Convergence Lattice
hazards.notes: A complex clockwork of bright metal and delicately carved gemstones, the lattice's interlocking gears begin to whir as golden runes glow across its …
hazards.stealth: +34 (master) to realize the lattice is a complex clockwork before it begins to move; noticing the lattice itself is DC 0.
hazards.disable: DC 40 Thievery (master) or DC 35 Religion (master) four times to obliterate each of the four key runes. A DC 45 Thievery (legendary) check (or breaking the lattice) stops the clockwork's movement and prevents it from resetting, but doesn't stop its current activation.
hazards.reset: The convergence lattice deactivates and resets after there are no uncontrolled targets within line of sight for 1 minute.

hazards.name: Corazal Aflame
hazards.notes: Fire burns Corazal and threatens to spread to the surrounding forest.
hazards.disable: DC 30 Nature or Survival (expert) to douse flames or DC 32 Athletics (expert) to smother flames; on the sixth successful check, the flames go out. Casting a non- cantrip water spell on the flames counts as one success.

hazards.name: Cordon Alarm
hazards.notes: A hempen rope tied between trees emanates an invisible, cylindrical barrier that sounds an alarm when crossed.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery (trained) to move the rope without setting off the alarm, or dispel magic (1st rank; counteract DC 16) to disable the rope’s magic
hazards.reset: The alarm resets immediately. Multiple breaches can cause the alarm to sound in multiple places at the same time, though the alarm can still be triggered only once per round.

hazards.name: Corpse Disposal
hazards.notes: A wooden trap door conceals a spike-filled pit 10 feet square and 20 feet deep. The DC to Climb out of the pit is 10.
hazards.stealth: DC 21 (or 0 if the trap door is disabled or broken )
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery (trained) to jam the trap door open

hazards.name: Corpselight Mist
hazards.notes: Churning vapors of glowing green mist fill a 30-foot-deep chasm.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Religion to counteract Kabriri's influence here by offering prayers to any non-evil deity and causing the mist to disperse, or dispel magic (3rd level; counteract DC 23) to counteract the mist for 24 hours
hazards.reset: The hazard resets automatically at the end of a turn and can trigger again the next round.

hazards.name: Corrupted Draft
hazards.notes: Discordant music, dance, and poetry combine to build a deep suspicion and distrust of strangers.
hazards.disable: Performance DC 28 to counteract the performance or Religion or Occult DC 28 to disrupt the spiritual energy. Two total successes are needed to disable the trap. The mechanical head can automatically disable the trap with two uses of Inspired Recitation.
hazards.reset: The hazard stops when there are no conscious creatures in area E3 and resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Covetous Corridor
hazards.notes: Statues depicting the runelords of envy steal magic from intruders.
hazards.disable: DC 45 Arcana (master) to unweave the magic surrounding a statue, DC 48 Athletics (expert) to wrest a statue’s implement from its hands, DC 48 Thievery (expert) to slip an implement free, or dispel magic (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the magic that empowers the statue. Increase the DCs to disable the Belimarius statue by 2. Each statue must be disabled or counteracted separately, and disabling the Belimarius statue or all nine other statues permanently disables the hazard. Belimarius Statue AC 42; Fort +34, Ref +28, Will +37 Belimarius Statue Hardness 31; HP 120 (BT 60); Immunities critical hits , object immunities , precision damage
hazards.reset: The hazard resets automatically if not disabled.

hazards.name: Cracked Earth
hazards.notes: This 20-foot-by-20-foot patch of ground is cobwebbed with cracks and fissures that crumble when a creature steps on it.
hazards.disable: DC 16 Survival (untrained) to collapse safely; DC 20 Crafting (trained) to shore it up enough to pass over without collapsing it

hazards.name: Crush the Uninvited
hazards.notes: A warning carved into the door frame magically crushes any who pass through the doorway without Kemnebi's permission.
hazards.stealth: DC 48 (legendary); 20 to notice the warning carved in the door frame
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to scratch out the warning or dispel magic (10th level; counteract DC 48) to counteract the magic in the warning

hazards.name: Crushing Gate Trap
hazards.notes: A hidden stone rod causes two immense stone doors to fall forward from their gate, crushing anything beneath them. The doors also fall forward if …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
hazards.stealth: DC 42 (master) to spot the triggering rod beneath the black sand
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 42 (expert) to secure the doors in place without triggering the trap

hazards.name: Crystal Pin
hazards.notes: Ebeshra fires a crystal at a creature to pin them onto the Material Plane .
hazards.disable: DC 48 Occultism (legendary) or Religion (legendary) to earn Ebeshra's favor and allow safe travel or DC 51 Deception (master) to momentarily divert Ebeshra's attention
hazards.reset: Ebeshra waits 1d4 rounds to break off another crystal.

hazards.name: Crystalized Agony
hazards.notes: A violet crystal containing the body of a dead creature, grown from its dying agony, pulses as it exudes motes of flickering energy.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Thievery (master) or DC 35 Survival (master) to know where to Strike a specific crystal perfectly on a facet to cause it to shatter harmlessly
hazards.reset: A crystallized agony resets automatically and can be triggered again the next round.

hazards.name: Cuastic Shower
hazards.notes: Contact with the doors, pillars, or statue causes a shower of acid.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Crafting (master) to ground the charged features or DC 50 Thievery (legendary) to disable the contact sensors

hazards.name: Daemonic Fog
hazards.notes: The fog solidifies into tiny, gnawing creatures that devour everyone within before fading back into mist.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Survival (expert) to disrupt the fog before the hazard triggers or dispel magic (5th level; counteract DC 26) to counteract the magic.
hazards.reset: The hazard resets over the course of an hour as the daemonic stain reenergizes the fog.

hazards.name: Dahak's Shell
hazards.notes: A ring of eight dragon pillar replicas mark the border of a dome of magical prismatic energy that entirely contains the Fortress of Sorrow.
hazards.disable: Each dragon pillar that is destroyed removes the corresponding color's effect from Dahak's shell; as long as even one color remains active, the pillars marking the shell's border cannot be damaged themselves, but a successful DC 32 Thievery (master) check or a successful dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 30) against one of the eight pillars can cause a randomly determined active color in the shell defense (below) to become deactivated for 1d4 rounds.

hazards.name: Dahak's Skull
hazards.notes: A pair of magical gems inside the dragon skull's eye sockets act as magical sensors with a 30-foot radius.
hazards.stealth: +0, but DC 24 to notice that the fiery lights within the skull's eye sockets seem to be looking around the room.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 27 (expert) two times to pry the gems embedded deep in the skull's eye sockets without triggering the sensor, or dispel magic (4th level, counteract DC 22) twice to dispel both eyes.

hazards.name: Damurdiel's Vengeance
hazards.notes: An elven woman wearing a robe stands in the water. She beckons anyone who enters the room to join her in the pool.
hazards.stealth: +37 (legendary) or DC 47 to notice the dagger left in the pool start to move on its own
hazards.disable: Deception 45 (legendary) to pretend to be Erveniss and ask for forgiveness, Diplomacy 45 (legendary) to convince Damurdiel to stand down ( elves who are masters in Diplomacy can attempt the check as if they were legendary instead), or Religion 40 (legendary) to call upon Calistria to calm Damurdiel's spirit.
hazards.reset: Damurdiel's spirit subsides once she is destroyed or if she manages to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points. She returns after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Dance of Death
hazards.notes: An eerie orchestra compels all who hear it to dance until they collapse from exhaustion.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Intimidation (expert) three times to frighten dancers and spectral musicians alike away from participating in the deadly performance, DC 40 Performance (master) twice to produce a tune discordant enough to disrupt the compulsion, or DC 42 Religion (master) three times to banish the spirits with prayers
hazards.reset: The eerie orchestra spends an hour retuning its phantasmal instruments, after which it is ready to begin its routine again.

hazards.name: Darkside Mirror
hazards.notes: A magic mirror replaces characters with malicious mirror duplicates from another dimension.
hazards.disable: DC 34 Thievery (legendary) to retrieve a creature from the other dimension within 10 minutes of the switch (possible only if their mirror duplicate is dead), DC 39 Thievery (master) to permanently disable the mirror once all mirror duplicates are dead, or dispel magic (7th rank; counteract DC 32) to counteract the mirror for 1 minute and prevent additional replacements during that time.
hazards.reset: The mirror is always ready to absorb creatures into the other dimension. Ten minutes after a creature is sucked into the mirror, if an ally doesn't rescue the creature, it reaches the other dimension. In the mirror dimension, it counts as a mirror duplicate. These dimensions are alternate realities, not planes, so even spells like <%SPELLS%1576%%>interplanar teleport<%END> can't reach them.

hazards.name: Dart Barrage
hazards.notes: Four dart-loaded pipes hidden in the diagonal walls are connected to a pressure plate under the brass seal in the room's center.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace
hazards.stealth: +11 (trained) or DC 23 (trained) to notice scratches around the musical pipes and a slight give to the seal
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 22 (trained) to disable the pressure plate, or four Thievery DC 18 (trained) checks to plug the dart launchers
hazards.reset: The trap runs out of darts after 4 rounds of firing and must be reset manually by dismantling the walls to reload the launchers. If at any point there are no longer more than two creatures placing weight on the floor, the trap ceases firing but remains armed, ready to resume firing its remaining darts once triggered again.

hazards.name: Dart Launcher
hazards.notes: A series of hidden launch tubes fire toxic darts at a 5-foot square.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 16 (trained)

hazards.name: Deadly Workshop
hazards.notes: Swinging bladed chains whip through the entire workshop.
hazards.stealth: +16 (expert) to notice the blades embedded in the chains and the complex system of pulleys connecting them
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 20 (expert) on the control panel on the raised platform deactivates the trap.
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Death's Slumber Ward
hazards.notes: A whirlwind of four ephemeral, magical threads dispels the undead and shrouds the living in an endless slumber.
hazards.disable: DC 23 Religion (expert) or DC 21 Performance (trained) to dissipate one of the four threads. Characters who failed or critically failed a Performance check to participate in Grandfather Eiwa's funeral in Chapter 1 have been able to reflect on the experience; these characters gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their Performance checks to disable this trap. The trap is destroyed when all four threads are dissipated.
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minute after no living or undead creatures are within 100 feet, then resets.

hazards.name: Deathly Dream
hazards.notes: Sinister runes adorn the doorway, opening a portal to a realm of nightmares if anyone other than Dwandek opens the door.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #173: Doorway to the Red Star
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 40 (master) to seal the rift using materials strongly grounded to the Material Plane , or dispel magic (7th-level, counteract DC 33) to counteract the portal.
hazards.reset: The deathly dream trap resets automatically as long as it hasn't been disabled or destroyed. Each time it resets, the tiny pocket plane of nightmare it sends its victim into resets as well, so no two victims will ever share the same deathly dream.

hazards.name: Decrepit Bridge
hazards.notes: The 30-foot-long, 10-foot-wide bridge groans under the weight of those who cross it.

hazards.name: Demilich Skull
hazards.notes: The skull of a defeated demilich is haunted by souls of the demilich's victims.
hazards.disable: DC 26 Arcana , Occultism , Nature , or Religion to counteract the skull's Broken Gems
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Desperate Hunger
hazards.notes: A skeletally thin spirit appears, weeping as it shoves earth and stones down its throat in an effort to stave off hunger.
hazards.stealth: DC 35 (master) to feel an odd sense of hunger
hazards.disable: DC 36 Deception (master) to convince the spirit it's no longer hungry or DC 38 Occultism (trained) to ritually feed the spirit
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Devil's Breath
hazards.notes: The taxidermy monster lurches forward, howls, and exhales a blast of foul-smelling smoke.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 23 to pluck out the taxidermy's gemstone eyes
hazards.reset: The Devil’s Breath resets automatically after an hour.

hazards.name: Dimensional Darkside Mirror
hazards.notes: A magic mirror replaces characters with evil mirror duplicates from another dimension.
hazards.stealth: +37 (master) to notice it isn't a regular mirror
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 40 (legendary) to retrieve a creature from the other dimension within 10 minutes of the switch (possible only if their mirror duplicate is dead), Thievery DC 45 (master) to permanently disable the mirror once all mirror duplicates are dead, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 37) to counteract the mirror for 1 minute and prevent additional replacements during that time
hazards.reset: The mirror is always ready to absorb creatures into the other dimension.
