hazards.disable: DC 36 Arcana , Nature , Occultism , or Religion (master) to convince the spirit that the target’s magical knowledge is too great to be trifled with
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Kepgeda's Keening Cauldron
hazards.notes: The cauldron's ear-splitting keening calls forth spectral claws to assail ears and souls alike.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Athletics to tip the cauldron, or DC 20 Occultism or Religion (trained) to ward against the cauldron's effects. Any combination of three successful attempts is required to fully disable the haunt. When the haunt is disabled, the coven seeks vengeance (see Coven's Vengeance)
hazards.reset: The haunt becomes inert (resuming its usual screaming) at the end of any round in which no creatures other than Kepgeda remain in her kitchen.

hazards.name: Keystone Repulsion
hazards.notes: Four magic keystones repel creatures when one is damaged or tampered with.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to remove each keystone or DC 48 Occultism (legendary) to manipulate the magic to isolate each keystone

hazards.name: Keystone Trap
hazards.notes: A 5-foot-square metal vault covered with knobs lies concealed within a stone block. A lever on the stone block slides the vault into view. When the …
hazards.disable: DC 24 Thievery (trained) to find and press hidden knobs in a specific order (three successes are required to disable the trap, which also opens it); DC 24 Crafting (expert) to sabotage the vault's mechanisms, reducing its actions by 1 (when the trap's actions are reduced to 0, it is disabled)

hazards.name: Killing Fugue
hazards.notes: A vision of a terrifying presence (the King in Yellow, the Crawling Chaos, or some other horror beyond imagining) overwhelms an unfortunate explorer, …
hazards.disable: DC 48 Diplomacy (master) to talk the affected individual out of the killing fugue, DC 45 Occultism (legendary) to recognize the spiritual attack taking place and help the victim to resist its effects; four successes are required to disable the nightmare
hazards.reset: As long as a creature remains under the effects of the nightmare, it cannot reset. Once a creature has either recovered from the effects or died, the nightmare resets in 1d4 rounds.

hazards.name: Krooth Summoning Rune
hazards.notes: The haze conceals a rune that summons a krooth in front of the door to area B10.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God
hazards.disable: DC 24 Acrobatics to approach without triggering the trap followed by DC 26 Thievery (expert) to erase the rune, or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 24) to counteract the rune
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 24 hours.

hazards.name: Kugaptee's Anger
hazards.notes: The sound of toppling trees and thunderous footsteps fills the air, as if some immense giant had taken notice and now slowly approaches through the …
hazards.disable: DC 23 Nature or Religion to offer prayers against the evil to reduce Kugaptee’s Anger’s actions during its routine to 1 (see below) for 1 round; placing Sui-Jing’s heart into her corpse at area A2 is the only way to disable this hazard

hazards.name: Kugaptee's Tree
hazards.notes: The branches of the stone tree statue animate, extend, and lash out at intruders.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Religion to exorcise the haunt, or DC 28 Intimidation to appear overwhelmingly strong of body and mind so that the haunt recoils and fades
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Last Prayers of the Doomed
hazards.notes: Influenced by the last prayers of the dead, creatures experience extreme claustrophobia and batter at the walls and floor, desperate to escape, see …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.stealth: DC 30 (expert) to hear desperate whispered prayers
hazards.disable: Religion DC 26 (expert) to disrupt the haunt through prayer, or Deception or Diplomacy DC 27 (expert) to convince the spirits you’ll free them from this place
hazards.reset: The haunt reforms after 1 day.

hazards.name: Lava Flume Tubes
hazards.notes: Four gated channels carved into stone allow lava to flow into a 15-foot-tall room; the floor can withdraw to allow the hardened lava to fall into a …
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 29 (expert) to block a channel, or Thievery DC 31 (master) to release the floor latch and escape to the chamber below
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 hour by withdrawing the floor, cracking and dumping the hardened lava (and any creatures trapped inside) into the chamber. Creatures <%RULES%402%%>fall<%END> 40 feet, taking falling damage (typically 17 bludgeoning damage).

hazards.name: Lesser Dragonstorm
hazards.notes: A small-scale version of a dragonstorm—a churning vortex of wind infused with fire, acid, lightning, poison, and ice—fills Alseta's Ring.
hazards.disable: Religion DC 40 (legendary) to call out to a non-evil deity for direct intervention to disperse the lesser dragonstorm (prayers to Apsu allow characters who are masters in Religion to attempt the check as if they were legendary instead), Thievery DC 42 (legendary) to deactivate Vengegate while the manifestation is forcing it open, or a successful dispel magic (10th level; DC 40) to counteract the lesser dragonstorm.

hazards.name: Lichen Monstrosity
hazards.notes: A mass of petrified lichen takes the shape of a beast and lurches forward.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Survival or Thievery (master) to scrape away lichen without being exposed, or DC 36 Medicine or Nature (expert) to concoct a natural remedy and weaken the hazard; four total successes are required to disable it
hazards.reset: The trap resets over the course of an hour.

hazards.name: Life Magnet
hazards.notes: A magical magnet hidden behind a panel in the corner of the room pulls not metal but living creatures toward it, heedless of any obstacles in the way.
hazards.disable: DC 29 Thievery (expert) to deactivate the panel, or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 22) to counteract the panel's magic
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets 1 minute after there are no creatures touching the iron bars.

hazards.name: Life-Draining Thunder
hazards.notes: Thassilonian runes set with onyx erupt with negative energy and thunderous roars at the presence of a living creature.
hazards.disable: DC 35 Thievery (master) to destroy the key rune, DC 37 Arcana (master) to harmlessly discharge the runes, or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 31) to counteract the trap

hazards.name: Lifeleech Crystal Patch
hazards.notes: Sharp, bloodthirsty crystals make walking through this chamber treacherous.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City
hazards.stealth: DC 30 (expert) or detect magic to note the presence of necromantic energies suffusing the crystals.
hazards.disable: Religion DC 30 (expert) to utter prayers that quell the crystals' necromantic compulsion to drink blood

hazards.name: Lightlock
hazards.notes: The strange fog layer on the walls swirls and churns, then suddenly fires several beams of dark mist into the room.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 27 (master) to disrupt some of the hidden runes that focus the trap's energies, or dispel magic (4th level, counteract DC 25) or any spell with the Light trait to counteract the trap

hazards.name: Lightning's Dance
hazards.notes: Electricity suffuses an area where Agyra has used her lightning breath multiple times.
hazards.stealth: +20 (expert) or DC 33 (master) to notice sparks dancing around normally non-conductive surfaces
hazards.disable: DC 35 Crafting (master) to fashion a makeshift lightning rod, DC 33 Nature (expert) to dissipate the electrical charge harmlessly into the air
hazards.reset: The hazard deactivates and immediately resets if has no targets for 1 round; it also resets if Agyra uses her lightning breath multiple times in a single combat in the area.

hazards.name: Locking Alarm
hazards.notes: Any attempt to open the door without first tracing the symbol of Yhidothrus (an hourglass) on the door's face with a fingertip causes a glowing green …
hazards.disable: DC 32 Thievery (expert) to bypass the magical triggers on the door, or dispel magic (5th level, counteract DC 29) to counteract the alarm.
hazards.reset: The locking alarm resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Locking Door
hazards.notes: A door (or other portal) slams shut and locks.
hazards.stealth: DC 18 to notice the door sway slightly, even though there's no breeze
hazards.disable: DC 14 Athletics to push back against the door, DC 14 Crafting to wedge the door open, or DC 20 Thievery (trained) to jam the lock or open the lock afterward

hazards.name: Lodestone Trap
hazards.notes: The magical lodestone discharges bolts of electricity that also magnetize metal in the room.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery to unhook the pressure plates from the trap, or dispel magic (2nd level, counteract DC 18) to counteract the trap
hazards.reset: At the end of a round in which there are no creatures standing on the floor or stuck to the lodestone, the trap deactivates. The vargouilles return to their alcoves, and the doors close. The trap resets automatically after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Lonely Machine Spirit
hazards.notes: Ghostly smoke rising from an alchemical engine belches forth; the screeching sound of grinding gears echoes from the engine as it shutters to life.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Religion (trained) or DC 20 Engineering Lore (trained) to eject the animating spirit from its mechanical shell. Creatures gain a +2 circumstance bonus on their check if they use the airship's name, Harpy's Kiss , as part of their skill check, or a +4 circumstance bonus if they utter the name “Phera Wyndslow.” The haunt remains active until its spirit is ejected, the haunt is destroyed, or there are no living creatures within 30 feet.
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates and resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Loose Slab
hazards.notes: The stone slab tears free from its track with the ear-piercing sound of failing metal.
hazards.disable: DC 20 Crafting (expert) to shore up the track so that it functions as intended, or DC 18 Thievery (trained) to wedge the slab in place to immobilize it.

hazards.name: Luminous Ward
hazards.notes: A burst of radiance explodes from the door.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 40 (master) to disable the wards or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 38) to counteract the ward
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Lyzerium Bottle
hazards.notes: Five tiny glass bottles, each full of volatile green liquid, are discretely positioned around the room. Each bottle explodes when its glass is broken.
hazards.disable: Interact action to pick up one of the five bottles

hazards.name: Maggot Pit
hazards.notes: Countless human-faced, fanged maggots wriggle and squirm in this chamber.
hazards.stealth: +0 (the maggots are slow and impossible to miss)
hazards.disable: Three DC 45 Religion checks within the room to utter prayers, which calm and quell the maggots with invocations to the gods
hazards.reset: The pit functions continuously. If it's disabled or destroyed, it resets automatically after 24 hours if the crystal stele in area M2 still functions, otherwise it doesn't reset.

hazards.name: Major Wards
hazards.notes: Layers of fulus and strips of prayer-printed ribbons are plastered over the walls and entrances to the manor, demarcating a boundary around the …
hazards.stealth: DC 32 (master) to recognize that the fulus function as magical wards; noticing the fulus that cover the manor walls is DC 0
hazards.disable: DC 35 Arcana , Occultism , or Thievery (master) to compromise the magic to allow entry into the manor, DC 32 Athletics to force your way through the barrier and enter the manor (this doesn’t allow other PCs to enter behind you, though!), or dispel magic (5th rank; counteract DC 28) to counteract the wards
hazards.reset: The wards reset automatically, continuing to prevent entry and damaging those who attempt to bypass them until they’re disabled.

hazards.name: Malevolent Mannequins
hazards.notes: A host of violent spirits possess three clockwork mannequins, and each lashes out at any creatures that dare walk near.
hazards.disable: DC 37 Thievery (master) to jam a mannequin's clockwork mechanisms or Religion DC 35 (expert) twice to exorcise a spirit from a mannequin.
hazards.reset: The haunt deactivates after it has no target creatures and resets, usually over the course of 1 round, as the mannequins move to their original positions. If a mannequin is more than 150 feet from its original position, the haunt takes longer to reset, as the mannequin moves back 150 feet each round.

hazards.name: Mana Whorl
hazards.notes: This 15-foot-wide patch of destabilized sand attempts to submerge creatures who wield magic. A desert tree with dense bright green foliage, pale pink …
hazards.stealth: +14 (trained) to identify as dangerous quicksand; +20 (expert) to recognize its magical properties
hazards.disable: DC 26 Arcana (expert) to feed magic into the whorl and temporarily stabilize it for a few minutes; feed the whorl a number of spellcasters and magic items with a combined 10 levels (for instance, a 4th-level cleric with two 3rd-level magic items) to stabilize it for 1 week; or feed the whorl a number of spellcasters and magic items with a combined 20 levels to stabilize it permanently. Spellcasters and magic items fed to the whorl are devoured whole.
hazards.reset: The hazard continues to suck in anyone with magic until it is satiated (see Disable above). Magpies leave any satiated whorls.

hazards.name: Masks of Aroden's Guises
hazards.notes: Ten masks adorn twelve stone statues.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God
hazards.disable: DC 29 Religion (expert) or Occultism or DC 31 Thievery (expert) to dismiss the magic on a single statue. Replacing the two missing masks (a mask made of or incorporating coins on the merchant statue and a mask made of any valuable fabric on the tailor statue) and succeeding at a DC 27 Religion check disarms the trap.
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets 1 minute after it has no target creatures.

hazards.name: Maze of Mirrors
hazards.notes: Invisible runes in the maze disorient those within it and cause its mirrored walls to shift about.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God
hazards.stealth: +18 (trained) to detect the magical runes in the maze; noticing the maze itself has a DC of 0
hazards.disable: DC 26 Thievery (expert) or dispel magic (5th level; counteract DC 28) to stop the mirrors' shuffling; DC 28 Occultism or Religion (expert) to dispel the minotaur
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any creature in the maze.

hazards.name: Meddler's Muddle
hazards.notes: A rune hidden in the door’s decorative carvings delivers a telepathic jolt, draining will and muddling the mind.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 26 (expert) to scratch out the rune without triggering a mental assault, or dispel magic (3rd rank; counteract DC 24) to counteract the rune
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Memory Hole
hazards.notes: Anyone looking into the hole has memories sucked from their head.
hazards.disable: DC 29 Deception (master) to feed the pit false thoughts that plug it, or DC 28 Occultism (expert) or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 27) to drain the pit's magic
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 hour if it's not disabled.

hazards.name: Memory of Osoyo
hazards.notes: The party’s memories of Osoyo coalesce into a titanic mirage in the storm clouds above.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Occultism (trained) or DC 24 Arcana (trained) to divert the memory’s rage; three total successful checks are required to disable the hazard

hazards.name: Mental Assault
hazards.notes: Magic sigils hidden in the grain of the wooden door trigger a magic trap that damages the mind of anyone attempting to pick the door's lock.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to deface the symbols or dispel magic (10th level, counteract DC 48) to counteract the trap.
hazards.reset: The trap resets automatically if triggered and doesn't reset if disabled.

hazards.name: Mental Scream Trap
hazards.notes: A psychic scream disorients creatures in the area.
hazards.disable: Arcana (DC 41) to suppress the magic or Thievery (DC 41) to scratch out the ward

hazards.name: Methane Flue
hazards.notes: Invisible but highly flammable natural gas has built up beneath the ground, where geological pressure can ignite it.
hazards.disable: Survival DC 28 to dig around the vent in a way that diffuses the fumes

hazards.name: Middenworm Infestation
hazards.notes: A dead body seems to ripple and bulge, as if something inside were shaking.
hazards.disable: DC 23 Medicine or DC 26 Thievery to carefully cut into the corpse and vent the worms harmlessly in a safe direction

hazards.name: Mindhammer Mushrooms
hazards.notes: The mushrooms emit powerful psychic blasts that overwhelm potential predators with exhausting psychedelic visions.
hazards.stealth: DC 20 (trained) to notice small animal skeletons among the mushrooms
hazards.disable: DC 20 Survival (trained) to navigate a safe path without triggering the mushrooms
hazards.reset: The mushrooms must rest for 24 hours before they can emit another Psychic Blast

hazards.name: Mirror Door
hazards.notes: The reflection of a wall shows a phantom door where none exists. This door can only be manipulated while viewed through the mirror's reflection.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery to open the door while viewing the reflection
hazards.reset: automatic

hazards.name: Mirror of Glory
hazards.notes: A reflective field of energy fills a large archway in a gatehouse, in which viewers regard themselves dressed in fine clothes, bowing down before …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star
hazards.disable: DC 37 Thievery (master) to disrupt one of the six anchor points that link the paradigm cube to the mirror, DC 34 Arcana (legendary) to use knowledge of magic that opposes pride to unravel the mirror’s power, DC 37 (master) Intimidation to use one’s force of personality to stand against the arrogance amplified by the mirror, or dispel magic (8th-rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract one of the six faces of the paradigm cube ; six successes are required to disable the Mirror of Glory
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates, then resets instantly.

hazards.name: Mist Projector
hazards.notes: Hidden jets expel gas that quickly freezes, causing limited damage to nearby books.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm
hazards.disable: DC 27 Thievery (expert) to deactivate the trap without its control key or DC 26 Crafting to create and apply a chemical that neutralizes the gas.
hazards.reset: 8 hours

hazards.name: Mogaru's Breath
hazards.notes: Mogaru exhales a blast of intense flames to eradicate any meddlesome pests in the area.
hazards.disable: DC 50 Performance (legendary) or DC 53 Deception (legendary) to momentarily divert Mogaru's attention
hazards.reset: Mogaru must wait 1d4 rounds before letting loose another gout of fire.

hazards.name: Mournful Petals Haunt
hazards.notes: A flurry of scattered flower petals flies through the area, as psychic impressions of pain, sorrow, and being trapped assail the living—Mirida’s …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: DC 31 Occultism or Religion (expert) to weaken the haunt, DC 29 Deception or Diplomacy (expert) to soothe the haunt’s sorrow; three total successes in any combination are required to disable the haunt.
hazards.reset: The petals disperse after 1 minute and reset after 1 day.

hazards.name: Mukradi Summoning Runes
hazards.notes: Barely visible runes are etched into the stone floor in a 20-foot diameter circle.
hazards.stealth: +25 (master) to notice runes marked on the floor.
hazards.disable: DC 36 Acrobatics to approach without triggering the trap followed by DC 34 Occultism (expert) or DC 38 Thievery (master) to erase the rune, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 34) to counteract the rune
hazards.reset: The trap resets at the first high tide of each day.

hazards.name: Myristica's Despair
hazards.notes: The illusion shatters, revealing the grove to be a lifeless scar and the seemingly peaceful loggers to be crawling aimlessly about the clearing, …
hazards.stealth: +13 (expert) to recognize that the scene before them is an illusion.
hazards.disable: DC 22 Nature (trained) to tame the primal energy, DC 23 Diplomacy (trained) to console the dryad, DC 24 Occultism (trained) to identify and heal the emotional wounds; three successes are required to disable the haunt.
hazards.reset: Unless Silene is destroyed, this haunt can recharge itself after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Names of the Nameless
hazards.notes: The voices of the nameless dead intrude into the minds of the living.
hazards.disable: DC 26 Perception to discern a name spoken by the nameless dead, or DC 28 Religion (expert) to put the nameless dead to rest. Speaking three names aloud disables the haunt. A creature that speaks any other name aloud must succeed at a DC 28 Will save or be confused for 1 round.
hazards.reset: If the haunt is disabled, divine light washes through the area. Living creatures in the area regain 4d8 Hit Points, and undead creatures in the area take 4d8 <%TRAITS%509%%>vitality<%END> damage. The haunt deactivates 1 minute after all creatures leave the area but resets immediately thereafter.

hazards.name: Night's Breath Trap
hazards.notes: The night giant mummy unfolds its arms and leans forward to exhale a blast of gray mist and shrieking spirits into the room.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Thievery to “blind” the statue so that it cannot notice any who approach, DC 35 Occultism to redirect and expend the trap's occult energies harmlessly, or dispel magic (7th level, counteract DC 32) to counteract the trap.
hazards.reset: The trap resets during the following round, after which it can be triggered again.

hazards.name: Nightmare Feast
hazards.notes: The consumption of sentient, and even sapient creatures is widespread in Leng. Those who suffer such fates are as much the genesis of this nightmare …
hazards.disable: DC 43 Society (master) to fight these destructive urges by focusing your thoughts on traditions not so steeped in cruelty, or DC 40 Intimidation (legendary) to overwhelm the nightmare’s influence with the strength of your own personality; three successes are required to disable the nightmare
hazards.reset: The nightmare deactivates as soon as a round begins with no creatures in its area, and resets in 1d6 rounds.

hazards.name: Nightmare Portal
hazards.notes: Horrific visions of a lumbering monstrosity whose face is nothing but a fanged mouth lurch out of the violet mist to attempt to eat the viewer alive.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Thievery (master) to focus the portal's energies back in on itself to close it off, or DC 36 Occultism (master) to invoke the proper chant and make the proper hand gestures to untether the portal from the Dreamlands , or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 34) to counteract the portal for 1 minute and prevent Orgesh's influence from reaching through during that time
hazards.reset: The nightmare portal resets 1 minute after it no longer detects targets.

hazards.name: Nosois' Vengeance
hazards.notes: The sparrow on the scroll animates, speaking to the PCs in Noguchi’s voice (one of the nosois from Event 11: Nosois’ Brunch ): “They’re the ones! …
hazards.disable: DC 36 Thievery (to quickly destroy the scroll without triggering the hazard), DC 33 Religion (to apologize to Pharasma and the nosois for the previous insult), or dispel magic (6th rank; counteract DC 29).

hazards.name: Nyrissa's Tempest
hazards.notes: Sudden dark clouds gather in the sky above, and moments later, blasts of lightning and swirling tornadoes begin to rip the landscape apart.
hazards.disable: Nature DC 42 (master) to note the magical nature of the storm and to perform a quick ritual and prayer to the fey spirits of the region to cause the tempest to disperse, or dispel magic (9th level, counteract DC 36) to counteract the tempest immediately.

hazards.name: Obscured Pitfalls
hazards.notes: A layer of disembodied eyes obscures a pitfall in the floor that's either deep enough for a human to fall into, or narrow enough to cause a painful …
hazards.stealth: DC 18 (or 0 if the eyes covering an area that obscures a pitfall are destroyed)
hazards.disable: This hazard can't be disabled, merely avoided.

hazards.name: Offended Epitaphs
hazards.notes: Funerary inscriptions flicker and display different messages, causing ghostly ancestors to briefly appear and complain that their descendants have …
hazards.disable: three DC 20 Diplomacy , Occultism , or Religion checks to rebuke the cantankerous spirits

hazards.name: Oil Explosion
hazards.notes: The flammable oil catches flame and explodes, burning up in a ball of fire.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Survival (trained) or DC 23 Crafting to neutralize the oil without setting it alight

hazards.name: Orb Blast Trap
hazards.notes: Five globes shoot bolts of force up and down the hall when a second creature reaches its midpoint.
hazards.stealth: +35 (master) to realize that the glimmering orbs signal a dangerous trap.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 48 (master) to deactivate the trap entirely before it triggers, Thievery DC 45 (expert) to deactivate one of the glimmering orbs after the trap rolls initiative, or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 41) to deactivate the trap entirely.
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates 1 round after it has no creatures to target and resets automatically after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Ornery Augdunars
hazards.notes: Spooked augdunars gallop wildly about the paddock, biting and kicking as they run.
hazards.disable: Succeed at four of the following checks in any combination: Nature DC 14 (trained) to calm the animals, Intimidation DC 16 (untrained) to scare the augdunars away, Will DC 18 (trained) to avoid flinching and project confidence, causing the augdunars to veer away. For each success, the hazard takes a cumulative –1 penalty to attack rolls.

hazards.name: Ostovite Nest
hazards.notes: A nest of bones resembling an ant hill contains countless miniscule scavenger vermin with vicious, acid-dripping mandibles.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Athletics (trained) to topple the mound and destroy it
hazards.reset: The hazard deactivates if there are no targets for its acid spew at the start of its turn. The hatchlings return to the nest, and the hazard resets. If damaged but not destroyed, the nest recovers 1d6 Hit Points per hour as the hatchlings repair it.

hazards.name: Pain Milker
hazards.notes: An eerie machine made of levers, crystals, and glowing bits of metal that, as one draws near, causes unsettling aches and pains.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Thievery (master) to deactivate the machine, or DC 38 Perception (expert) to decipher the proper order in which the switches and dials should be adjusted in order to power the device down harmlessly
hazards.reset: If the <%MONSTERS%776%%>augnagar<%END> still lives and at least one <%HAZARDS%245%%>crystallized agony<%END> is still functional, the pain milker resets automatically in a number of rounds equal to 7 – the number of remaining crystallized agonies.

hazards.name: Painful Suggestion Trap
hazards.notes: A hidden rune on the floor under the filth, just past the threshold, triggers an ersatz ghost.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (expert) to remove the rune without triggering it, or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 26) to dispel the rune
hazards.reset: The trap automatically resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Paradox Engine
hazards.notes: All six sides of this adamantine -reinforced box are covered with Thassilonian runes. Touching a rune allows one to exchange its position with …
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 41 (expert) to feel the subtle vibrations when moving a rune to shift into the right position, or Thassilon Lore DC 33 (expert) or Society DC 38 (master) while being able to read Thassilonian to work out the anagram puzzle using traditional means, or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 34)
hazards.reset: The paradox engine deactivates 1 minute, and its owb prophet returns to its interior after all creatures leave the area, but resets immediately thereafter.

hazards.name: Paralysis Trap
hazards.notes: Magical symbols carved in the doorframe magically ward this door; anyone attempting to pick the lock is paralyzed and wracked with pain. Disabling or …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 28 (expert) to scratch out the magical symbols, Arcana DC 28 (expert) to safely siphon the magical energy, or dispel magic (4th rank; counteract DC 26); Bypass Anyone other than Mirida turns the door handle three times to the right and once to the left in quick succession.
hazards.reset: The trap automatically resets. It doesn’t reset if the trap is disabled.

hazards.name: Paralyzing Light Trap
hazards.notes: When any creature other than a devil enters the light, the magic interwoven in the light holds the creature in place and rings an alarm.
hazards.disable: Disable DC 26 Thievery (master) to distort or diffuse the light, keeping the light cone intact but preventing the trap from triggering, or dispel magic (4th level; counteract DC 26) to dispel the light, leaving the room in darkness

hazards.name: Scholar's Bane
hazards.notes: Illusions overwhelm the minds of particularly intelligent creatures, forcing them to relive every intellectual failure and shame they’ve ever …
hazards.stealth: +14 (trained) to notice magical sensors hidden within four of the carvings’ eyes
hazards.disable: DC 22 Thievery (trained) to carve out one eye sensor, DC 22 Arcana or Occultism (trained) to blank out one’s mind (disables trap for self only), or dispel magic (2nd rank; counteract DC 20) to counteract one eye sensor
hazards.reset: The trap can function for 10 rounds, which don’t need to be consecutive, before it must recharge for 24 hours.

hazards.name: Scythe Blades
hazards.notes: Two blades, each hidden in a 15-foot-long ceiling groove, are both connected to a trip wire.
hazards.disable: DC 21 Thievery (trained) to disable each blade
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 15 minutes.

hazards.name: Second Chance
hazards.notes: Powerful warding magic tied to an object or location tries to regress the ages of a creature and its allies.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 46 (legendary) to take apart the spell one tiny piece at a time, with eyes closed, while recalling every vivid life memory in order, starting from the earliest memory

hazards.name: Second Kiss Engine
hazards.notes: Exposed clockwork gears spin at high speeds.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (expert) to disable the engine, or DC 26 Engineering Lore to disengage the drive shaft. Either method disables the trap but also shuts down the engine, disabling the Second Kiss's propulsion.

hazards.name: Seismic Spears Trap
hazards.notes: Lines of searing lava lance through the area, causing targets to shake as if caught in an earthquake and potentially become petrified.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 43 (master) to disable the wards or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 38) to counteract the ward.
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Serpent Ward
hazards.notes: Illusionary snakes erupt from the trapped door, inflicting a venomous curse on intruders.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind
hazards.disable: DC 26 Thievery (expert) or DC 24 Occultism (expert) to deactivate the magical trigger

hazards.name: Shadow Discharge
hazards.notes: The shadow beacon’s operation causes harmful energy to blast out of the base of the device.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: DC 27 Crafting or Thievery (master) to rig a dispersal system, or DC 27 Arcana , Nature , Occultism , or Religion (master) to safely vent the magical energy; four total successes in any combination to disable

hazards.name: Shadow Guards
hazards.notes: Shadowy caricatures of elves peel themselves from the floor and attack everyone in the room.
hazards.stealth: +11 (trained) to notice the runes concealed among the drawings
hazards.disable: DC 16 Acrobatics to move through the room without touching the runes, followed by DC 18 Thievery (trained) to carve them out without triggering them; or dispel magic (1st rank; counteract DC 16) to counteract the runes
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute. The drawings cannot pursue characters out of the room.

hazards.name: Shadow Heart
hazards.notes: A heart of tumorous, shadowy tissue unleashes magic on nearby creatures.
hazards.disable: DC 26 Arcana or Occultism (expert) to counter the heart's offensive magic, or DC 28 Religion (trained) to purify the area containing the heart. Four successes are required to disable it; after two successes, the shadow heart can't use its shadow lash Strike.
hazards.reset: The heart deactivates if there are no creatures present in the room. It resets in 1 hour.

hazards.name: Shadow Hook
hazards.notes: Hooks of solidified shadow extend from the walls, hook into creatures, and pull, tearing them open.
hazards.disable: DC 50 Thievery (legendary) to disable the trap's sensors

hazards.name: Shadow Lash
hazards.notes: Four pillars manifest shadow lashes that attack intruders.
hazards.disable: DC 46 Arcana (legendary) to drain the magic from each shadow lash or DC 48 Thievery (legendary) to disable each shadow lash

hazards.name: Shadow Maze
hazards.notes: Shifting illusions disorient, entrap, and agonize those who attempt to pass through the shadowy maze.
hazards.stealth: +32 (master) to realize the water within the dome poses a supernatural threat
hazards.disable: DC 42 Thievery (master) to decouple faint strands of shadow essence from the magical matrix that holds the maze together, DC 45 Arcana or Occultism to shunt the shadowy energy back into the Shadow Plane and render the maze inert, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 35) to counteract the shadow maze
hazards.reset: If disarmed, the trap resets in 1 hour as long as the two crystals in area C5 still function.

hazards.name: Shadow Roil
hazards.notes: A cyclone of living shadows and planar magic surges around the area, attracted to living creatures.
hazards.disable: DC 32 Arcana or Occultism (expert) to weaken the tornado; three successes in any combination are required to disable the trap.
hazards.reset: The cyclone disperses after 1 minute and resets after 1 day.

hazards.name: Shadows of Everglut
hazards.notes: Swirling shadows that behave like animated pools of ink splash and slither up against the limbs of those who tread too far into this chamber.
hazards.disable: Three DC 33 Arcana or Occult checks to redirect the negative energy back in on itself and disrupt the hazard's source of power, a DC 36 Religion check to offer prayers to sever the sacred link to Kabriri, or dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 29) to render the hazard inert for 10 minutes
hazards.reset: The hazard settles back down 1 round after all creatures leave the room and can trigger again at the start of the next round.

hazards.name: Shadowshift Field
hazards.notes: Cross-planar see page from the Oaksteward rebels’ ritual causes shadowy warping effects to strain and damage living creatures in the forest clearing.
hazards.stealth: +7 (trained) to notice the air and plants wavering and shifting
hazards.disable: DC 17 Arcana (trained) to will the Universe’s hold on the area back into firmness and disable the effect for 1 hour, or dispel magic (1st rank; counteract DC 15) to end the effect permanently
hazards.reset: This effect continues for 1 day, after which it ends and cannot be triggered again without another ritual.

hazards.name: Shaken Loose
hazards.notes: The Granite Ox shakes off centuries of accumulated earth, flinging the PCs toward its hindquarters.

hazards.name: Shattered Runewell of Pride
hazards.notes: Plumes of magenta and violet light and vapor shift and writhe out of a hole in reality surrounded by the fragments of a runewell suspended …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star
hazards.disable: DC 37 Arcana (master) or DC 40 Occultism (master) to redirect the magic back in on itself and cancel out the danger, or DC 40 Crafting (legendary) to reposition runewell fragments so they’re not dangerous; three total successes are required to disable the shattered runewell

hazards.name: Shattered Window
hazards.notes: The anger trapped within a structure shatters a window, showering glass in adjacent spaces.
hazards.stealth: DC 17 (trained) to notice cracks spider-webbing across the window
hazards.disable: DC 19 Occultism or Religion (trained) to suppress the spiritual energy or DC 20 Diplomacy (trained) to soothe the latent anger

hazards.name: Shattering Rune
hazards.notes: A magical rune is inscribed on the tarry earth at the entrance to the hut, buried beneath snow, with an invisible sensor that detects creatures …
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 30 (master) to erase the rune without triggering the sensor or dispel magic (5th level; counteract DC 28) to dispel the rune

hazards.name: Shelyn's Shame
hazards.notes: The statue begins to weep, its tears running in rivulets down into the surrounding pool, filling all nearby with overwhelming shame and grief.
hazards.stealth: DC 33 (master) to notice tears beginning to run from the statue’s eyes
hazards.disable: DC 29 Religion (master) to offer prayers to Shelyn (a worshipper of Shelyn gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check), or DC 33 Diplomacy (expert) to offer condolences and comforts to the haunt

hazards.name: Shocking Malfunction
hazards.notes: The shadow beacon malfunctions, firing bolts of electricity across the battlefield.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: DC 25 Crafting or Thievery (master) to ground the device, or DC 25 Arcana , Nature , Occultism , or Religion (master) to safely vent the magical energy; three total successes in any combination to disable

hazards.name: Shrieker
hazards.notes: This human-sized purple mushroom emits a piercing shriek when disturbed.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Survival to carefully approach and cut the mushroom’s air sac without triggering the shrieker
hazards.reset: 1 minute

hazards.name: Shrieking Souls
hazards.notes: A terrified soul releases an earsplitting scream.
hazards.disable: DC 44 Diplomacy (master) to comfort the spirit or DC 45 Occultism (master) to ward off the spirit
hazards.reset: 1 hour.

hazards.name: Shrinking Hall
hazards.notes: This hallway is designed to shrink as creatures traverse it, making access to the door at the hall's end impossible.
hazards.disable: DC 21 Thievery (trained) to jam the scales built into the floor
hazards.reset: After 10 minutes without weight being placed on this hall's floor, this trap resets, returning the hall to its original size.

hazards.name: Shroud of Silence
hazards.notes: Sounds become muted in a 20-foot-wide, 100-foot-long segment of this street corridor.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Occultism (expert) to twist the magic of the ley line around you, disabling the hazard for only you; or dispel magic (4th rank; counteract DC 23) to disable the hazard permanently

hazards.name: Shrouded Assailant
hazards.notes: A spirit steps out of a covered mirror, pulling off and becoming shrouded in the cloth, which reveals the mirror. The shrouded figure attacks the …
hazards.disable: DC 43 Thievery (master) to steal the cloth before the spirit manifests, or DC 47 Athletics to pull the cloth off the spirit after it manifests
hazards.reset: The haunt can be reset if the mirror is covered in a cloth or shroud.

hazards.name: Shuffling Hall
hazards.notes: Four pressure plates along this mirrored hall rotate vertically when stepped on, sending a creature on the pressure plate tipping into an adjacent …
hazards.disable: DC 12 Thievery to deactivate one pressure plate
hazards.reset: automatic

hazards.name: Shuffling Scythe Blades
hazards.notes: Six long blades, hidden in grooves in the walls and floor, zigzag through different parts of this hallway when any pressure plate in the hallway …
hazards.disable: DC 26 Thievery (expert) to disable each blade, or utter the magical passphrase (which only Chafkhem knows) to deactivate the trap for 10 minutes
hazards.reset: The trap resets when no creatures remain in area B20. Damaged or destroyed blades aren’t repaired when the trap resets.

hazards.name: Sickle Blades
hazards.notes: A skeletal arm holding a sickle is concealed in the ceiling and connected to a mechanism in the sliding door below it.
hazards.disable: DC 20 Thievery (trained) on the door frame or ceiling groove, or Interact to operate a lever on the opposite side of the door (in areas D2 and D4, respectively)
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 15 minutes. Additionally, a creature can manually Interact with the lever on the opposite side of the door to reset the trap.

hazards.name: Sigil of Deepest Fears
hazards.notes: An arcane sigil forces creatures to confront their greatest fear.
hazards.disable: DC 43 Thievery (master) to drain the sigil's power harmlessly, or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 42) to counteract the sigil
hazards.reset: 1 day

hazards.name: Silvered Retribution
hazards.notes: Pressure plates in the floor, wall, and ceiling of this hall trigger silver blades to protrude from the ceiling, slashing anything passing through …
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 28 (master) to disable the pressure plates; two successes are required to disable the trap
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates after 1 minute and can be manually reset.

hazards.name: Siphoning Spirit
hazards.notes: A formless spirit drains life from the living, becoming progressively visible as its victims weaken.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Occultism or Religion (expert) to weaken the spirit; four total successes are required to disable the haunt
hazards.reset: After 1 minute, the spirit is satiated, and the haunt deactivates as it returns to a resting state. Over the course of 1 hour, the spirit's siphoned life energy disperses and the haunt resets.

hazards.name: Skewering Hall
hazards.notes: A dozen spears hidden within sockets in the walls thrust into the hall when the pressure plate is triggered.
hazards.disable: DC 47 Thievery (master) to disable the pressure plate

hazards.name: Skulls of Fear and Flame
hazards.notes: A line of skulls adorned with black candles sit on the floor, and use darkvision to spot intruders. The red arrows on the map indicate the direction …
hazards.stealth: +17 (expert) to notice little wisps of smoke start to curl up from the unlit candles on the skulls.
hazards.disable: Stealth DC 27 to move through the room unseen by the skulls (this does not disable the trap but does prevent it from triggering), Thievery DC 27 three times to “blind” an adjacent skull by deftly scraping hidden runes away from the inside of the eye sockets, or dispel magic (4th level, counteract DC 25) to counteract the trap
hazards.reset: If there are no visible targets, the trap deactivates at the end of its turn, then automatically resets.

hazards.name: Slamming Door
hazards.notes: Pressure-sensitive panels in the floor connect to a stone slab hidden in a hallway’s ceiling.
hazards.disable: DC 15 Thievery (trained) on the floor panels before the slab falls

hazards.name: Slamming Gate
hazards.notes: The heavy gate slams shut when opened more than halfway.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 15 (trained) to loosen the gate's springs before it slams closed
hazards.reset: The trap can be reactivated (or deactivated, if it's active) by flipping a lever hidden in the nearby wall. A character <%ACTIONS%519%%>Searching<%END> the area finds it with a successful DC 18 Perception check.

hazards.name: Slothful Stairs
hazards.notes: A supernatural exhaustion fills creatures who climb the stairs.
hazards.disable: DC 45 Athletics (legendary) to wedge crumbling stones into cracks to jam the collapsing stairs, DC 48 Thievery (master) to deface the hidden magical runes that power the trap; or dispel magic (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract a rune; three total successes are required to disable the trap
hazards.reset: The trap continues taking Leaden Limbs actions (and the void at the bottom of the stairwell remains open) for as long as creatures remain in the area. Once no creatures remain, the stairwell rebuilds itself, the void closes, and the trap resets.

hazards.name: Smith's Skull
hazards.notes: The smith's skull gazes with fiery light and breathes in a deep breath.
hazards.stealth: DC 42 (master) to see the skull's lower jaws start to open
hazards.disable: DC 48 Athletics (master) to hold the skull's jaw shut, or DC 45 Occultism or Religion (expert) to quiet the Smith's spirit
hazards.reset: 1 hour

hazards.name: Smoke-Filled Hallway
hazards.notes: Thick smoke fills this hallway, making it difficult to see and breathe.
hazards.disable: While a spell like gust of wind can temporarily clear a path through the smoke, the hazard returns at the start of the next round as long as the fires in area A17 continue to burn; DC 18 Survival to know how best to cover your nose and mouth with a wet cloth to help alleviate the choking effects of the smoke.
hazards.reset: The smoke continues to affect anyone who enters area A16 until the fires in area A17 are extinguished.

hazards.name: Snake's Mane
hazards.notes: A tangle of feathery green vines appears innocuous but fires a spray of acidic barbs at anything that disturbs it.
hazards.stealth: DC 27 (trained) to discern the snake’s mane from the surrounding vegetation
hazards.disable: Disable DC 27 Nature (expert) to strip the barbs from the vines, rendering them harmless, or DC 30 Stealth (trained) to move through the snake’s mane without disturbing it
hazards.reset: 1 hour, as the vine grows a new set of barbs

hazards.name: Snowfall
hazards.notes: Loose snow and ice have built up on a high surface, such as a tree branch or a rooftop. Its grip on the surface is tenuous, and it is likely to fall …
hazards.disable: DC 19 Survival (trained) to safely dislodge the snow, or deal any amount of fire damage to destroy the hazard without triggering it

hazards.name: Soporific Lecture
hazards.notes: Several hidden nozzles spray colorless sleeping gas into the seating area.
hazards.disable: DC 28 Thievery (expert) to crimp shut the primary feeding tube for the gas, or DC 31 Perception (expert) to discover the hidden bypass switch next to the door to area A3 that shuts the trap off

hazards.name: Soul Draining Cage
hazards.notes: Necromantic runes inscribed on the cage bars and lock drain the vitality of living creatures who interact with the cage.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 25 (expert) to drain the runes power harmlessly or dispel magic (3rd level; counteract DC 22) to counteract the rune

hazards.name: Soul Stasis
hazards.notes: Four steel pillars emit pulsing energy to slow souls' processes.
hazards.disable: DC 43 Arcana or Religion (master) to reweave the magic within each pillar, DC 46 Thievery (master) to disable each pillar, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 43) to counteract each pillar
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any souls in the area.

hazards.name: Soul-Draining Spirit Collectors
hazards.notes: Four spirit collectors drain the souls from nearby creatures.
hazards.disable: DC 47 Religion (legendary) to sever the connection between Urgathoa and each spirit collector, DC 50 Thievery (legendary) to deactivate each spirit collector, or dispel magic (9th level; counteract DC 50) to counteract each spirit collector

hazards.name: Spear Launcher
hazards.notes: A wall socket loaded with a spear connects to a floor tile in one 5-foot square.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery (trained) on the floor tile or wall socket

hazards.name: Spectral Archers
hazards.notes: Ghostly soldiers wielding crossbows manifest within the towers that flank the gatehouse and rain bolts down upon intruders.
hazards.disable: DC 31 Intimidation (expert) to cow the archers into fleeing or DC 28 Religion (expert) to temporarily banish the spirits
hazards.reset: The haunt vanishes permanently if the graveknights are destroyed. Otherwise, it returns after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Spectral Reflection
hazards.notes: The reflection in the mirror subtly twists and distorts, its expression taking on an unnerving sneer of malice.
hazards.disable: DC 23 Religion (trained) to exorcise the spirit, or DC 23 Thievery (trained) to quickly cover the mirror
hazards.reset:
The haunt re-forms after 1 minute, manifesting in any mirror within its infused area (see Special Below).

Special Spectral reflections often infuse entire buildings, manifesting in any sufficiently large mirror. The example Hit Points and Hardness given represent a typical mirror reinforced by the haunt; at your discretion, the haunt might appear in reflective surfaces that are harder to destroy. Defeating a manifestation through damage destroys the surface, preventing the haunt from using it again. If this haunt appears in an area with many mirrors, consider giving PCs double or even triple the XP for a typical simple hazard.

hazards.name: Spell Pitchers
hazards.notes: A large pitcher plant occupying a 5-foot space sits seemingly dormant with its dull petals open.
hazards.stealth: DC 20 (trained) to recognize the plant among others
hazards.disable: DC 15 Arcana (trained) to safely trigger the plant's reflexes, causing it to close and become dormant for one day, or DC 17 Nature (trained) to carefully coax the pitcher into quiescence
hazards.reset: Once the pitcher has eaten a spell, its petals turn dark pink and green before it closes. It goes dormant for one day per spell level of the spell consumed. Once the pitcher finishes digesting, it opens again and slowly wilts. A second pitcher branches into an adjacent square when the first pitcher opens again.

hazards.name: Spider Summoning Rune
hazards.notes: An invisible rune on the floor summons a goliath spider when disturbed by someone who isn't wearing Norgorber's religious symbol .
hazards.disable: DC 34 Thievery (master) to erase the rune or dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 36) to dispel the rune.
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 24 hours.

hazards.name: Spike Launcher
hazards.notes: A jagged spike of metal shoots from a hidden launcher.
hazards.disable: DC 16 Thievery to disable one of the four launchers or DC 12 Acrobatics to step over a trip line (this doesn’t disarm the trap, but avoids triggering it)

hazards.name: Spike Thrower
hazards.notes: Slats in the ceiling open and pepper the chamber below with long, metal spikes fired from spring-loaded tubes.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery to jam the gears and prevent the trap from being activated

hazards.name: Spiked Barricade Trap
hazards.notes: Spring-loaded wedges of sharpened stone pop out of the wooden barricade.
hazards.disable: DC 33 Thievery (expert) to suppress the spring mechanism for one 5-foot segment of the barricade
hazards.reset: The trap must be manually reset by pushing the wedges back into place.

hazards.name: Spiked Doorframe
hazards.notes: Spikes lance out of the doorframe to skewer anyone who attempts to open the door.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 20 (trained) to deactivate a trigger built into the door's handle

hazards.name: Spiky Pit Trap
hazards.notes: A piece of hide covered with a layer of dirt and gravel is suspended over a 20-foot pit filled with spikes.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Thievery (trained) to manually trigger the trap without falling in, or DC 25 Thievery (trained) to secure the hide so the trap doesn't activate
hazards.reset: Creatures can still fall into the trap, but the hide that covers it must be reset manually (a 10-minute activity) for the trap to become hidden again.

hazards.name: Spinning Blade Pillar
hazards.notes: A metal pole with three razor-sharp spinning blades is hidden in the floor, connected to trigger plates in up to eight floor tiles and a hidden …
hazards.stealth: +11 (trained) or DC 26 (expert) to notice the control panel
hazards.disable: DC 21 Thievery (trained) twice on the pillar, or DC 19 Thievery (expert) once on the control panel deactivates the whole trap. Breaking the control panel prevents anyone from disabling the trap using the control panel and prevents the trap from deactivating automatically (see Reset below).
hazards.reset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.

hazards.name: Spiral Seal
hazards.notes: A spiral shape suggesting the curling religious symbol of Pharasma is carved into the stone floor.
hazards.disable: DC 37 Occultism (master) or DC 40 Religion (master) to unmake the Spiral Seal through occult ritual or prayer performed as a 10 minute activity with the Concentrate trait, or dispel magic (9th level, counteract DC 40) to counteract the Spiral Seal.
hazards.reset: Recovery <%ACTION.TYPES#6%%> Frequency once per round; Trigger The Spiral Seal is damaged but is above its Broken Threshold; Effect The Spiral Seal repairs itself, regaining 30 Hit Points.

hazards.name: Spiraling Comets
hazards.notes: Three blue comets orbiting the room turn red and attack when intruders enter.
hazards.disable: DC 42 Religion (master) to command each comet to disperse with Pharasmin prayers, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 42) to counteract each comet
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 1 hour.

hazards.name: Spirit Cyclone
hazards.notes: A cyclone of angry spirits surges around the area.
hazards.disable: DC 30 Occultism or Religion (trained) to weaken the haunt; three total successes in any combination are required to disable the haunt
hazards.reset: The spirit cyclone disperses after 1 minute and resets after 1 day.

hazards.name: Spirit Window
hazards.notes: Spirits trapped inside a haunted window harm those who touch the window.
hazards.disable: DC 48 Occultism (legendary) to free the spirits from the mirror, or DC 48 Religion (legendary) to banish the spirits
hazards.reset: 1 round

hazards.name: Spiritual Disruptor
hazards.notes: A flickering humanoid shape with four gold eyes, clad in red robes with black sleeves and wielding a torch that burns with red fire and smoke, …
hazards.disable: DC 23 (expert) Intimidation to disrupt the haunt’s concentration in the living world and break its link to the mindscape, DC 27 (expert) Religion to banish the energy from the mindscape, or DC 30 (expert) Occultism to turn the haunt’s energy back against itself to cancel it out
hazards.reset: If both hazards are disabled or destroyed, a new one forms adjacent to a randomly determined character still inside the crumbling building after 1d4+2 rounds. Once all three NPCs are rescued or exorcised, these hazards don’t reset.

hazards.name: Spitter Pods
hazards.notes: Specialized spore pods burst open, expel toxic globules, and recharge from alchemical reservoirs.
hazards.disable: DC 18 Crafting to add disruptive chemicals to the fungus's reservoir, DC 18 Nature (trained) to recognize how to constrict the chemicals' flow, or DC 20 Deception (trained) to spread spores that befuddle the fungus; three total successes are required to disable the trap.

hazards.name: Spitting Daffodils
hazards.notes: Daffodils spit acidic nectar at non-plant creatures in the area.
hazards.disable: DC 25 Thievery (expert) or DC 25 Survival (trained) to remove the plant's motion sensing filaments
hazards.reset: The daffodils replenish their nectar and filaments after 24 hours.

hazards.name: Sportlebore
hazards.notes: A sportlebore hides amid victuals on a plate of food or within a pack of trail rations.
hazards.disable: A creature that notices the sportlebore can remove it from the food it’s hidden within automatically as an Interact action.

hazards.name: Stabbing Sentinels
hazards.notes: A petrified creature momentarily animates to attack an adjacent creature.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands
hazards.disable: DC 40 Thievery (master) to remove the animating magic without triggering the trap, or dispel magic (8th level; counteract DC 38) to counteract the animating magic
hazards.reset: The magical energy that animates the statue builds up again over 24 hours and the trap resets.

hazards.name: Stage Fire
hazards.notes: Flames engulf the opera house's stage.
hazards.disable: Survival DC 27 to extinguish two adjacent squares of fire (with a critical success extinguishing four adjacent squares); any water spell (such as from create water or hydraulic push ) cast at the fire extinguishes two squares automatically, or 2d4 adjacent squares if the caster of the spell achieves a DC 30 result with a spell attack roll; quench instantly extinguishes all fire within its 20-foot burst.

hazards.name: Steam Vents
hazards.notes: Large pressurized pipes connected to a trip wire are rigged to release a blast of steam on trespassers.
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 22 (trained) to disconnect the trip wire or Crafting DC 24 (expert) to carefully reduce the pressure and prevent the blast

hazards.name: Sticky Greeter
hazards.notes: A taxidermy giant spider’s abdomen opens up to spray the area in front of it with sticky webbing.
immunity: precision damage Web Hardness 5; Web HP 20; Immunities bludgeoning damage
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 23 to disable the pressure plate that triggers the sticky greeter

hazards.name: Stinger Ward Trap
hazards.notes: A ghostly stinger appears in the air and jabs at anyone moving through the opening.
hazards.disable: DC 36 Thievery (master) to prevent the ghostly stinger from forming or dispel magic (6th level; counteract DC 34).
hazards.reset: The trap resets after 24 hours.

hazards.name: Stinging Nettles
hazards.notes: This bright green plant has long triangular leaves covered with fine hair-like stingers.
hazards.disable: DC 17 Survival to carefully navigate the plant and pull aside or cut away the nettles

hazards.name: Stink-Sap Trap
hazards.notes: A nozzle attached to a pressure sensor under the flagstone path sprays thick wads of smelly sap.
hazards.disable: DC 15 Thievery (trained) to clog the nozzle or DC 14 Athletics (trained) to redirect the stream away from the path; the Athletics check can be made at a distance with a thrown object, but a critical failure triggers the trap's Sudden Spray.
hazards.reset: 1 minute. The trap resets automatically twice before the supply of stink sap is exhausted.

hazards.name: Stinkface Surprise
hazards.notes: A pile of excrement and rotten food is launched at whoever opens the trunk without first depressing a hidden button on the side of the trunk.
hazards.source: Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun
hazards.stealth: DC 27 (expert; DC 31 to detect the hidden bypass button)
hazards.disable: Thievery DC 26 (expert) to unhook the launch spring

hazards.name: Town Hall Fire
hazards.notes: A fire engulfs the western door and a 10-foot-by-10-foot area immediately east of it, then spreads on each of its turns.
hazards.disable: Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the flames. Water typically clears a 5-foot square if the amount is small (such as that from create water or hydraulic push ). Larger amounts of water, such as a full bucket, typically douse a 10-foot-by-10-foot area (or 4 squares in some other shape). Throwing a bucket of water on flames requires an Interact action. A waterskin doesn't contain enough water to put out even 1 square of fire. Cold can also put out fire, but only if the cold can affect an area; cold is usually less effective than water, so a frost vial typically puts out 1 square of fire, and ray of frost is ineffective. Fountain Circle, located outside town hall, has several working water pumps. These are far enough away that it's impractical for a PC to bring water back and forth. However, a PC might instruct the more steely nerved spectators to create a bucket brigade. It takes 15 spectators (which can include those rescued by councilors as well as by PCs) to set this up, and 2 rounds for the townspeople to line up and begin pumping water from Fountain Circle. As of the 3rd round, there is a bucket of water available for the PCs to use at the chamber's southern entrance at the beginning of each PC's turn. Members of a bucket brigade are lined up outside the chamber, and don't take damage from smoke inhalation. If a PC does want to carry the water, it's 150 feet from the chamber's southern door to a pump, so it 6 actions are usually needed to reach the pumps or return. Filling a bucket requires an Interact action. Other methods might also help control the fire, as you determine. For example, the PCs might be able to find something to barricade the fire with to control its path, or use a cloak to beat out some of the fire.

hazards.notes: The former bank manager's ghostly presence tempts creatures to partake in a dubious meal.
